Baseline: the unmodified stereovision2 under this run's VPR settings (regime 'koios_medium': channel width 300, device koios_medium, seed 1) has a critical path of 12.4624 ns and uses 219 DSP tiles of the device's 770, one block per tile. Its used logic-block area is 9.53973e+07 minimum-width transistor areas (one DSP tile 253779, one cluster 27905), so its area-delay product is 1.18888e+09. Its slowest stage is in my_fir: one hard multiply on a DSP tile (two_mult_18x19), then six adder levels with their carry chains, then one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop. The next slowest stage, in a different my_fir instance (endpoint group $dffe~788, not path 1's $dffe~456), is the same shape as path 1 — one hard multiply on a DSP tile, six adder levels with their carry chains, one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop, 12.297 ns, so shortening the slowest stage past that point buys nothing on its own. Any path your rewrite creates is compared against that critical path.

Rewrite rules

A stage is the logic between one register and the next. A block is one instance of the target mode. These rules hold for any synchronous design on any FPGA. Numbers that depend on this architecture are in the last section; use them, do not restate them as rules.

Must hold

Going against these produces a wrong design, not a slower one.

Observability. Only a block's output is visible. A value read by anything other than the arithmetic being taken into the block (another expression, a module output port, another module) cannot go inside a block. Keep it outside, or recompute it for those readers. Check the source; detection does not see port consumers. Operands are exempt: the block takes a copy and the original signal still exists.

Register control. A register carries its reset, enable and initial value. These modes hold no registers, so taking a register inside deletes that behaviour. If anything depends on it, keep the register and drive it from the block's result, or leave the site alone.

Arithmetic. The block computes the mode's expression on signed ports. Match the original bit for bit or leave the site alone.

design operandon a signed portallowed
unsigned, narrower than the portzero-extendyes
unsigned, as wide as the port, range provably below the signed maximum (constant coefficient, bounded value)zero-extend, state the bound and where it comes fromyes
unsigned, as wide as the port, range not boundable from the source (a top-level input)no exact representationno
original truncates each product before the suma fused sum truncated after differsno
original's narrow sum register wrapsthe low bits of the wider result reproduce the wrapyes
Weigh

The clock period is the delay of the slowest stage in the whole design. A stage's delay is the sum of everything on it: each block's fixed delay, each wire, each soft cell. Each relationship below names what it does to delay and to area. If a plan goes against one, say why.

1. Slowest stage → all outputs

Your task names the design's slowest stage and what is on it.

Slowest stage → delay

Relationship: A rewrite that does not touch the slowest stage cannot make the design faster, and must leave every stage no slower than it was. A rewrite that does touch it must make it shorter, not merely different. Compare every stage you change against it.

Slowest stage → area

Relationship: A rewrite that cannot shorten the clock period is paid for in tiles alone. Say so in the plan.

2. Block to register → delay

Relationship: A block's result goes to a register, or into the next block, with nothing but wire between. Any soft arithmetic between a block and its register is added to the stage.

3. Blocks in series → all outputs
Blocks in series → delay

Relationship: Each block in series adds its own delay plus one wire. Sum them with the wire in and the wire out, and compare against the slowest stage. That comparison, not a fixed count, says how many fit.

Blocks in series → area

Relationship: None. Series or side by side, the same blocks take the same tiles.

4. Arithmetic inside the block → all outputs

Arithmetic inside the block is what the mode's expression computes rather than what sits in series with it: a multiply and one addend, or two products and their sum, depending on the mode.

Arithmetic inside the block → delay

Relationship: Free. The block's delay is the mode's own and does not rise because its adder is used. This is where a conversion wins: soft logic leaves the stage and the block's delay already covers the work. An adder feeding the block's addend port is mapped into the block; an adder reading the block's result is on the path after it (rule 2). A block whose addend port is tied to a constant takes in nothing; if the multiply it replaces is already on a tile, the conversion changes the tile count and nothing else.

Arithmetic inside the block → area

Relationship: Flip-flops fall where product registers go. Do not count on LUT savings.

5. Registers → all outputs
Registers → delay

Relationship: A register may move only if no stage becomes longer and the module's latency is unchanged. If one must be added to keep latency, put it where it splits the longest stage. Every other operand entering that stage must be delayed by the same amount, or the stage adds values from different cycles.

Registers → area

Relationship: A register placed mid-chain costs operand-delay registers that a register after the chain does not.

6. Tiles → area

Relationship: A block occupies one DSP tile in one mode. Do not assume the multiply it replaces frees a tile: the synthesis tool may already have placed that multiply on a tile shared with others. Count the blocks against the tiles the unmodified design uses and the device's count, both in your task.

Every DSP mode costs the same 2.14 ns. The invented modes have no chain ports, so a partial sum passes between blocks through general routing. The packer can place up to four multiplies of 9 bits or less on one tile and up to two of 18 bits or less; a block in either invented mode takes its tile alone.

Before you commit to a plan

State in your plan: how many blocks and how many tiles on top of the unmodified design's; the longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay from the table, against the slowest stage; and what soft logic leaves the stage you touch, and whether that stage is the slowest one. If a site does not fit under those numbers, arrange it differently, take fewer, or leave it, and name the rule that ruled it out.

Objective: minimize the design's area-delay product, VPR's used area times the critical path, against the baseline in your task. A rewrite that does not lower it is not worth making; say so and output TIER: NONE rather than convert sites for their own sake. Among rewrites that lower it, prefer the one that lowers it most.

Classify the tier of the change you propose (a datatype/algorithm variant, T3, is out of scope —
do not propose one):

  • T1: Direct replacement: no change to the computed function or surrounding structure; no datatype change.
  • T2: Local restructuring only; preserve the region's function, role, and live consumers; no new operation/datatype family.

Why this region. The task names the slowest stage as a my_fir stage: one 18x19 hard multiply, six soft adder levels with carry chains, one LUT, into the enabled dout flip-flop. The second-slowest stage (12.297 ns) is the same shape in another my_fir instance. Rule 1 therefore forces converting all seven my_fir modules, not one: shortening a single instance buys nothing because the others hold the period at 12.297 ns. All 41 my_fir multiply/mult_add/sop candidates already feed a common reduction — the single dout sum inside their own module — so they are a legitimate sum-of-products fusion, not products feeding separate outputs.

What changes, per module. Replace the single dout <= expression with ceil(terms/2) comb_sop_2_18 instances wired as in MAPPING, then a balanced soft add of their result[27:0] values, assigned to dout inside the existing if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) branch. Seven-term modules (f1, f2, h2) go from 6 adder levels to 2 ((b0+b1)+(b2+b3)); six-term modules (f3, h1, h3, h4) go from 5 adder levels to 2 ((b0+b1)+b2). Write the tree explicitly parenthesized so synthesis does not linearize it back into a chain.

Soft logic that leaves the slowest stage. Four adder levels (f1/f2/h2) or three (f3/h1/h3/h4) with their carry chains leave the critical stage. The stage becomes: clk-to-Q 0.06 + register-to-block wire 2.25 + block 2.14 + block-into-soft-logic wire 1.48 + two adder levels 2×1.08 + the enable LUT and its wire ≈1.08 → ≈9.2 ns, against the 12.4624 ns baseline. Longest series of blocks in any stage is 1 — comb_sop_2_18 has no chain/addend port, so the four partial sums must meet in general routing and soft adders (rule 3 does not bind here; rule 2 does, and those two adder levels are counted above). The untouched fltr_compute multiply stage (register → 9x9 tile → q register ≈ 0.06+2.25+2.14+2.25 = 8.70 ns) becomes the floor, so 9.2 ns is the realistic period and no stage I touch ends up above it.

Area. Baseline: 219 tiles. The fltr_compute 9x9 group occupies 54 of them (consistent with 222 surviving 9x9 cells after fltr_compute_f2/fltr_compute_h2 CSE — identical coefficients on identical din, stereovision2.v:889-895 vs 992-998); the remaining 165 hold my_fir's 246 two_mult_18x19 cells one or two to a tile. Those 165 go away and 144 single-occupancy blocks take their place: 198 tiles, 21 fewer than baseline, well inside the device's 770. DSP area 198×253779 = 5.025e7; holding clusters at the baseline's ~1427 (3.982e7) as a conservative floor — the deleted adder chains should reduce it — gives ≈9.01e7 used area. ADP ≈ 9.01e7 × 9.2 ns ≈ 8.3e8 against the baseline 1.18888e9, roughly a 30% reduction. Even at a pessimistic 10.5 ns the ADP still falls to ≈9.5e8.

  • Registers (rule 5). Nothing moves. n_delay_reg1..6, dout and output_data_ready keep their new_data_rdy enable and their positions; the blocks are combinational and sit inside the existing stage. Module latency is unchanged, so my_fir_rdy_*/vidin_out_reg_* capture in h_fltr (stereovision2.v:523-529) is untouched.
  • Observability. din and n_delay_regN are read by the delay chain as well as the sum, but they enter the blocks only as operands, which is exempt — the registers still exist and still drive the chain. dout is the module's only arithmetic output and is driven from the block results.
  • Arithmetic exactness. Each tap is 16-bit unsigned into an 18-bit signed port: zero-extension is exact. Each coefficient is a positive constant ≤255 on a 19-bit signed port. The block sums the pair at full width with no intermediate truncation, matching Verilog's full-width product-then-sum. Worst-case total is f2/h2: (4+42+163+255+163+42+4)×65535 = 44,105,055 < 2^28, and every other module is smaller (f1 525×65535, f3 474×, h1 466×, h3/h4 348×), so dout <= sum_of_result[27:0] is bit-identical to the baseline's 32-bit sum truncated to the 28-bit register — no wrap in either version. All 42 fltr_compute multiply candidates — fltr_compute_f1 lines 859-865, f2 890-894, f3 928-934, h1 959-965, h2 993-997, h3 1030-1036, h4 1065-1071 — are left unconverted, for one shared reason with two parts. PLAN:

Why this region. The task names the slowest stage as a my_fir stage: one 18x19 hard multiply, six soft adder levels with carry chains, one LUT, into the enabled dout flip-flop. The second-slowest stage (12.297 ns) is the same shape in another my_fir instance. Rule 1 therefore forces converting all seven my_fir modules, not one: shortening a single instance buys nothing because the others hold the period at 12.297 ns. All 41 my_fir multiply/mult_add/sop candidates already feed a common reduction — the single dout sum inside their own module — so they are a legitimate sum-of-products fusion, not products feeding separate outputs.

What changes, per module. Replace the single dout <= expression with ceil(terms/2) comb_sop_2_18 instances wired as in MAPPING, then a balanced soft add of their result[27:0] values, assigned to dout inside the existing if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) branch. Seven-term modules (f1, f2, h2) go from 6 adder levels to 2 ((b0+b1)+(b2+b3)); six-term modules (f3, h1, h3, h4) go from 5 adder levels to 2 ((b0+b1)+b2). Write the tree explicitly parenthesized so synthesis does not linearize it back into a chain.

Soft logic that leaves the slowest stage. Four adder levels (f1/f2/h2) or three (f3/h1/h3/h4) with their carry chains leave the critical stage. The stage becomes: clk-to-Q 0.06 + register-to-block wire 2.25 + block 2.14 + block-into-soft-logic wire 1.48 + two adder levels 2×1.08 + the enable LUT and its wire ≈1.08 → ≈9.2 ns, against the 12.4624 ns baseline. Longest series of blocks in any stage is 1 — comb_sop_2_18 has no chain/addend port, so the four partial sums must meet in general routing and soft adders (rule 3 does not bind here; rule 2 does, and those two adder levels are counted above). The untouched fltr_compute multiply stage (register → 9x9 tile → q register ≈ 0.06+2.25+2.14+2.25 = 8.70 ns) becomes the floor, so 9.2 ns is the realistic period and no stage I touch ends up above it.

Area. Baseline: 219 tiles. The fltr_compute 9x9 group occupies 54 of them (consistent with 222 surviving 9x9 cells after fltr_compute_f2/fltr_compute_h2 CSE — identical coefficients on identical din, stereovision2.v:889-895 vs 992-998); the remaining 165 hold my_fir's 246 two_mult_18x19 cells one or two to a tile. Those 165 go away and 144 single-occupancy blocks take their place: 198 tiles, 21 fewer than baseline, well inside the device's 770. DSP area 198×253779 = 5.025e7; holding clusters at the baseline's ~1427 (3.982e7) as a conservative floor — the deleted adder chains should reduce it — gives ≈9.01e7 used area. ADP ≈ 9.01e7 × 9.2 ns ≈ 8.3e8 against the baseline 1.18888e9, roughly a 30% reduction. Even at a pessimistic 10.5 ns the ADP still falls to ≈9.5e8.

Preservation.

  • Registers (rule 5). Nothing moves. n_delay_reg1..6, dout and output_data_ready keep their new_data_rdy enable and their positions; the blocks are combinational and sit inside the existing stage. Module latency is unchanged, so my_fir_rdy_*/vidin_out_reg_* capture in h_fltr (stereovision2.v:523-529) is untouched.
  • Observability. din and n_delay_regN are read by the delay chain as well as the sum, but they enter the blocks only as operands, which is exempt — the registers still exist and still drive the chain. dout is the module's only arithmetic output and is driven from the block results.
  • Arithmetic exactness. Each tap is 16-bit unsigned into an 18-bit signed port: zero-extension is exact. Each coefficient is a positive constant ≤255 on a 19-bit signed port. The block sums the pair at full width with no intermediate truncation, matching Verilog's full-width product-then-sum. Worst-case total is f2/h2: (4+42+163+255+163+42+4)×65535 = 44,105,055 < 2^28, and every other module is smaller (f1 525×65535, f3 474×, h1 466×, h3/h4 348×), so dout <= sum_of_result[27:0] is bit-identical to the baseline's 32-bit sum truncated to the 28-bit register — no wrap in either version. The *0 terms the source already drops (COEF3_d, COEF3_1, COEF3_3, COEF3_4) stay dropped; no term is invented and no pre-adder or coefficient folding is introduced, so every product on a block is a product the design already computes.
  • Introduced operations/datatypes: NONE. Only re-association of an existing sum (hence T2, not T1).

Candidates left alone. All 42 fltr_compute multiply candidates — fltr_compute_f1 lines 859-865, f2 890-894, f3 928-934, h1 959-965, h2 993-997, h3 1030-1036, h4 1065-1071 — are left unconverted, for one shared reason with two parts. (a) Register control: each product lands in its own register q1..q7 (stereovision2.v:847-853) before the shared d_out_tmp sum, so a product pair does not reach a common reduction within one stage; fusing two products into one block deletes one of those registers and changes the module's structure. (b) Area with no delay return: these are 9x9 multiplies packed four to a tile on 54 tiles, while a comb_sop_2_18 block takes a tile alone — converting them would need ~111 tiles, +57 over baseline (~+1.45e7 area), and neither of fltr_compute's two stages is the slowest (multiply stage ≈8.70 ns, sum stage ≈4.8 ns), so per rule 1 the change would be paid for in tiles alone and would raise the ADP.

Risks. (1) The block-to-soft-adder wire and the final enable LUT are sampled ranges; if placement lands them near the high end the stage could reach ~11 ns instead of 9.2 — still below the 12.4624 ns baseline, and the ADP still improves because tiles also fall. (2) Synthesis may flatten the parenthesized two-level tree into a 3-deep chain; the tree must be written with explicit intermediate wires per pair. (3) The 144 blocks are single-occupancy, so if the packer's actual baseline split of my_fir across the 165 tiles differs from the 81/84 two-per/one-per reconstruction above, the tile delta could be nearer zero than −21; the delay win carries the ADP either way.

PLAN:

Why this region. The task names the slowest stage as a my_fir stage: one 18x19 hard multiply, six soft adder levels with carry chains, one LUT, into the enabled dout flip-flop. The second-slowest stage (12.297 ns) is the same shape in another my_fir instance. Rule 1 therefore forces converting all seven my_fir modules, not one: shortening a single instance buys nothing because the others hold the period at 12.297 ns. All 41 my_fir multiply/mult_add/sop candidates already feed a common reduction — the single dout sum inside their own module — so they are a legitimate sum-of-products fusion, not products feeding separate outputs.

What changes, per module. Replace the single dout <= expression with ceil(terms/2) comb_sop_2_18 instances wired as in MAPPING, then a balanced soft add of their result[27:0] values, assigned to dout inside the existing if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) branch. Seven-term modules (f1, f2, h2) go from 6 adder levels to 2 ((b0+b1)+(b2+b3)); six-term modules (f3, h1, h3, h4) go from 5 adder levels to 2 ((b0+b1)+b2). Write the tree explicitly parenthesized so synthesis does not linearize it back into a chain.

Soft logic that leaves the slowest stage. Four adder levels (f1/f2/h2) or three (f3/h1/h3/h4) with their carry chains leave the critical stage. The stage becomes: clk-to-Q 0.06 + register-to-block wire 2.25 + block 2.14 + block-into-soft-logic wire 1.48 + two adder levels 2×1.08 + the enable LUT and its wire ≈1.08 → ≈9.2 ns, against the 12.4624 ns baseline. Longest series of blocks in any stage is 1 — comb_sop_2_18 has no chain/addend port, so the four partial sums must meet in general routing and soft adders (rule 3 does not bind here; rule 2 does, and those two adder levels are counted above). The untouched fltr_compute multiply stage (register → 9x9 tile → q register ≈ 0.06+2.25+2.14+2.25 = 8.70 ns) becomes the floor, so 9.2 ns is the realistic period and no stage I touch ends up above it.

Area. Baseline: 219 tiles. The fltr_compute 9x9 group occupies 54 of them (consistent with 222 surviving 9x9 cells after fltr_compute_f2/fltr_compute_h2 CSE — identical coefficients on identical din, stereovision2.v:889-895 vs 992-998); the remaining 165 hold my_fir's 246 two_mult_18x19 cells one or two to a tile. Those 165 go away and 144 single-occupancy blocks take their place: 198 tiles, 21 fewer than baseline, well inside the device's 770. DSP area 198×253779 = 5.025e7; holding clusters at the baseline's ~1427 (3.982e7) as a conservative floor — the deleted adder chains should reduce it — gives ≈9.01e7 used area. ADP ≈ 9.01e7 × 9.2 ns ≈ 8.3e8 against the baseline 1.18888e9, roughly a 30% reduction. Even at a pessimistic 10.5 ns the ADP still falls to ≈9.5e8.

Preservation.

  • Registers (rule 5). Nothing moves. n_delay_reg1..6, dout and output_data_ready keep their new_data_rdy enable and their positions; the blocks are combinational and sit inside the existing stage. Module latency is unchanged, so my_fir_rdy_*/vidin_out_reg_* capture in h_fltr (stereovision2.v:523-529) is untouched.
  • Observability. din and n_delay_regN are read by the delay chain as well as the sum, but they enter the blocks only as operands, which is exempt — the registers still exist and still drive the chain. dout is the module's only arithmetic output and is driven from the block results.
  • Arithmetic exactness. Each tap is 16-bit unsigned into an 18-bit signed port: zero-extension is exact. Each coefficient is a positive constant ≤255 on a 19-bit signed port. The block sums the pair at full width with no intermediate truncation, matching Verilog's full-width product-then-sum. Worst-case total is f2/h2: (4+42+163+255+163+42+4)×65535 = 44,105,055 < 2^28, and every other module is smaller (f1 525×65535, f3 474×, h1 466×, h3/h4 348×), so dout <= sum_of_result[27:0] is bit-identical to the baseline's 32-bit sum truncated to the 28-bit register — no wrap in either version. The *0 terms the source already drops (COEF3_d, COEF3_1, COEF3_3, COEF3_4) stay dropped; no term is invented and no pre-adder or coefficient folding is introduced, so every product on a block is a product the design already computes.
  • Introduced operations/datatypes: NONE. Only re-association of an existing sum (hence T2, not T1).

Candidates left alone. All 42 fltr_compute multiply candidates — fltr_compute_f1 lines 859-865, f2 890-894, f3 928-934, h1 959-965, h2 993-997, h3 1030-1036, h4 1065-1071 — are left unconverted, for one shared reason with two parts. (a) Register control: each product lands in its own register q1..q7 (stereovision2.v:847-853) before the shared d_out_tmp sum, so a product pair does not reach a common reduction within one stage; fusing two products into one block deletes one of those registers and changes the module's structure. (b) Area with no delay return: these are 9x9 multiplies packed four to a tile on 54 tiles, while a comb_sop_2_18 block takes a tile alone — converting them would need ~111 tiles, +57 over baseline (~+1.45e7 area), and neither of fltr_compute's two stages is the slowest (multiply stage ≈8.70 ns, sum stage ≈4.8 ns), so per rule 1 the change would be paid for in tiles alone and would raise the ADP.

Risks. (1) The block-to-soft-adder wire and the final enable LUT are sampled ranges; if placement lands them near the high end the stage could reach ~11 ns instead of 9.2 — still below the 12.4624 ns baseline, and the ADP still improves because tiles also fall. (2) Synthesis may flatten the parenthesized two-level tree into a 3-deep chain; the tree must be written with explicit intermediate wires per pair. (3) The 144 blocks are single-occupancy, so if the packer's actual baseline split of my_fir across the 165 tiles differs from the 81/84 two-per/one-per reconstruction above, the tile delta could be nearer zero than −21; the delay win carries the ADP either way.

  • my_fir_f3 (1602-1607), my_fir_h1 (1661-1666), my_fir_h3 (1775-1780), my_fir_h4 (1833-1838): 6 terms → 3 blocks; pairs (din,r1) (r2,r4) (r5,r6). dout <= sop_sum01 + res2[27:0].

Each block gets a 16-bit unsigned tap zero-extended to the 18-bit signed ax/bx port ({2'b00, tap}) and that tap's coefficient as a positive constant on the 19-bit signed ay/by port; result[27:0] feeds the adder tree. No terms invented — the COEF3=0 taps the source already omits stay omitted. Delay-line registers, new_data_rdy enable, output_data_ready, dout width/latency, and every other module (including all fltr_compute_* multiplies) are unchanged.

Verification

  • bash check.sh stereovision2.v: OK: synthesizes cleanly. Census: comb_sop_2_18 144 (24 per h_fltr × 6 instances), $mul 498 → 252 (the 246 my_fir multiplies are gone; the remaining 252 are fltr_compute), $add 532 → 406.
  • Icarus sim with a behavioral comb_sop_2_18 (out = ax*ay + bx*by) against the original tap-sum expressions, 2000 random inputs, all seven modules: errors=0.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Inner-loop check: syntax + elaboration + cell census. NOT place-and-route.
3	# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
4	# Runs plain yosys (read_verilog; hierarchy; proc; opt; stat) on the one file: no arch, no
5	# parmys, no hard-block library. Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole
6	# design (the last "Number of cells" table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub,
7	# registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated
8	# module by name, which is where a hard-block instantiation such as comb_mult_add_16 shows up
9	# with its instance count.
10	set -u
11	f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
12	out="$(yosys -p "read_verilog $f; hierarchy -auto-top; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
13	rc=$?
14	if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
15	  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
16	  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
17	  echo "$out" | tail -10
18	  exit 1
19	fi
20	echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
21	echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
22	echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
23	                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
24	                   on {on=0}
25	                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
26	  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

Baseline: the unmodified stereovision2 under this run's VPR settings (regime 'koios_medium': channel width 300, device koios_medium, seed 1) has a critical path of 12.4624 ns and uses 219 DSP tiles of the device's 770, one block per tile. Its used logic-block area is 9.53973e+07 minimum-width transistor areas (one DSP tile 253779, one cluster 27905), so its area-delay product is 1.18888e+09. Its slowest stage is in my_fir: one hard multiply on a DSP tile (two_mult_18x19), then six adder levels with their carry chains, then one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop. The next slowest stage, in a different my_fir instance (endpoint group $dffe~788, not path 1's $dffe~456), is the same shape as path 1 — one hard multiply on a DSP tile, six adder levels with their carry chains, one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop, 12.297 ns, so shortening the slowest stage past that point buys nothing on its own. Any path your rewrite creates is compared against that critical path.

Rewrite rules

A stage is the logic between one register and the next. A block is one instance of the target mode. These rules hold for any synchronous design on any FPGA. Numbers that depend on this architecture are in the last section; use them, do not restate them as rules.

Must hold

Going against these produces a wrong design, not a slower one.

Observability. Only a block's output is visible. A value read by anything other than the arithmetic being taken into the block (another expression, a module output port, another module) cannot go inside a block. Keep it outside, or recompute it for those readers. Check the source; detection does not see port consumers. Operands are exempt: the block takes a copy and the original signal still exists.

Register control. A register carries its reset, enable and initial value. These modes hold no registers, so taking a register inside deletes that behaviour. If anything depends on it, keep the register and drive it from the block's result, or leave the site alone.

Arithmetic. The block computes the mode's expression on signed ports. Match the original bit for bit or leave the site alone.

design operandon a signed portallowed
unsigned, narrower than the portzero-extendyes
unsigned, as wide as the port, range provably below the signed maximum (constant coefficient, bounded value)zero-extend, state the bound and where it comes fromyes
unsigned, as wide as the port, range not boundable from the source (a top-level input)no exact representationno
original truncates each product before the suma fused sum truncated after differsno
original's narrow sum register wrapsthe low bits of the wider result reproduce the wrapyes
Weigh

The clock period is the delay of the slowest stage in the whole design. A stage's delay is the sum of everything on it: each block's fixed delay, each wire, each soft cell. Each relationship below names what it does to delay and to area. If a plan goes against one, say why.

1. Slowest stage → all outputs

Your task names the design's slowest stage and what is on it.

Slowest stage → delay

Relationship: A rewrite that does not touch the slowest stage cannot make the design faster, and must leave every stage no slower than it was. A rewrite that does touch it must make it shorter, not merely different. Compare every stage you change against it.

Slowest stage → area

Relationship: A rewrite that cannot shorten the clock period is paid for in tiles alone. Say so in the plan.

2. Block to register → delay

Relationship: A block's result goes to a register, or into the next block, with nothing but wire between. Any soft arithmetic between a block and its register is added to the stage.

3. Blocks in series → all outputs
Blocks in series → delay

Relationship: Each block in series adds its own delay plus one wire. Sum them with the wire in and the wire out, and compare against the slowest stage. That comparison, not a fixed count, says how many fit.

Blocks in series → area

Relationship: None. Series or side by side, the same blocks take the same tiles.

4. Arithmetic inside the block → all outputs

Arithmetic inside the block is what the mode's expression computes rather than what sits in series with it: a multiply and one addend, or two products and their sum, depending on the mode.

Arithmetic inside the block → delay

Relationship: Free. The block's delay is the mode's own and does not rise because its adder is used. This is where a conversion wins: soft logic leaves the stage and the block's delay already covers the work. An adder feeding the block's addend port is mapped into the block; an adder reading the block's result is on the path after it (rule 2). A block whose addend port is tied to a constant takes in nothing; if the multiply it replaces is already on a tile, the conversion changes the tile count and nothing else.

Arithmetic inside the block → area

Relationship: Flip-flops fall where product registers go. Do not count on LUT savings.

5. Registers → all outputs
Registers → delay

Relationship: A register may move only if no stage becomes longer and the module's latency is unchanged. If one must be added to keep latency, put it where it splits the longest stage. Every other operand entering that stage must be delayed by the same amount, or the stage adds values from different cycles.

Registers → area

Relationship: A register placed mid-chain costs operand-delay registers that a register after the chain does not.

6. Tiles → area

Relationship: A block occupies one DSP tile in one mode. Do not assume the multiply it replaces frees a tile: the synthesis tool may already have placed that multiply on a tile shared with others. Count the blocks against the tiles the unmodified design uses and the device's count, both in your task.

PLAN:

What changes. Each my_fir_* is re-associated into three pipeline stages that reproduce the same transfer function with the same latency. Writing d(τ) for din at enabled cycle τ (all registers advance only on new_data_rdy, so τ counts enabled cycles), the baseline computes dout(τ+1) = Σ_k d(τ-k)·C_k. Every coefficient set here is symmetric (C6=C0, C5=C1, C4=C2), and the f3/h1/h3/h4 sets drop the centre tap (C3=0, its product is already absent from the source), so:

  • T <= din + n_delay_reg4 gives T(τ) = d(τ-1)+d(τ-5), the taps that share C1=C5.
  • U <= din + n_delay_reg2 gives U(τ-1) = d(τ-2)+d(τ-4), the taps that share C2=C4, evaluated one cycle earlier where Z is built.
  • Z <= U*C2 + n_delay_reg2*C3 + n_delay_reg5*C0 (7-tap) or Z <= U*C2 + n_delay_reg5*C0 (6-tap), so Z(τ) carries exactly the k=2,3,4,6 (resp. k=2,4,6) terms of the sum due at τ.
  • dout <= din*C0 + T*C1 + Z supplies k=0,1,5 and the carried partial.

Summing these gives Σ_{k} d(τ-k)·C_k term for term; only the association order changes, which is exact because every operand and coefficient is non-negative and nothing is truncated before the final 28-bit assignment (largest coefficient sum is 673 for f2/h2, 673·65535 = 4.4e7 < 2^28, so no partial sum and no block result exceeds 28 bits and result[27:0] is the exact value). n_delay_reg6 becomes dead and is deleted; n_delay_reg1..5 keep the shift chain. T, U and Z are written under the same new_data_rdy enable as everything else, so the enable and hold behaviour is unchanged, and with power-up zeros the startup transient matches the baseline's as well.

Live inputs/outputs preserved. The module ports are untouched: dout is still a 28-bit register written one enabled cycle after the sample it summarizes, and output_data_ready is unchanged, so the top-level capture if (my_fir_rdy_x) vidin_out_reg_x <= vidin_out_temp_x (lines 525-540) and everything downstream in steer_fltr see identical values at identical cycles. T, U, Z are new internal registers with no other readers; nothing that leaves the module is taken inside a block. No register that anything depends on is deleted except n_delay_reg6, which has no reader after the rewrite.

Numbers I am committing to. 102 blocks (3 each in f1/f2/h2, 2 each in f3/h1/h3/h4 → 17 per instance group × 6 instances), down from the 144 blocks of the kept rewrite. Blocks take a tile alone, so DSP tiles go 200 → 158, i.e. 61 fewer than the unmodified design's 219 and 42 fewer than the kept rewrite, worth −1.07e7 min-width transistor areas. The longest series of blocks in any stage is one: every stage is register → one block → at most one soft adder → register, so no block-to-block routing hop exists anywhere. Worst stage from the table: clock-to-Q 0.06 + register-to-block wire 1.31 + block 2.14 + block-into-soft wire 1.38 + one 28-bit carry chain ≈ 0.5 + the trailing wire/LUT into the flip-flop seen in the measured report (2.43 + 0.15) + setup 0.02 ≈ 8.0 ns; without that trailing LUT it is ≈ 7.7 ns. The T/U pre-add stages are register → 17-bit add → register ≈ 4.1 ns, and the 6-tap Z stage is register → block → register ≈ 5.8 ns, both well clear.

What leaves the slowest stage. The kept rewrite's critical stage is one block followed by two soft adder levels ($add~572 then the 21-bit $add~573) and then the LUT into $dffe~580. This rewrite removes one of those two levels — the 1.00 ns inter-adder wire plus its ~0.49 ns carry chain — by cutting each FIR's stage down to a single block plus a single 28-bit add, which is possible because the folded pair sums (T, U) and the older taps (Z) arrive already registered rather than being built combinationally in the same stage. Yes, this is the slowest stage: every remaining my_fir instance has the same shape, and all 42 are rewritten identically, so none is left behind to hold the period at 9.14 ns.

Candidates left, with reasons.

  • All 42 fltr_compute_ multiply candidates (lines 859-865, 890-894, 928-934, 959-965, 993-997, 1030-1036, 1065-1071), left:* these seven 8-bit × ≤9-bit products per instance do feed a common reduction (d_out_tmp), so they would be legal to fuse, but they currently pack four to a tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt on 54 tiles. Fusing them into comb_sop_2_18 would need ~4 blocks per instance × 42 = 168 tiles that each block holds alone, i.e. +114 tiles ≈ +2.9e7 area, and their stage is not the slowest one, so by the slowest-stage/area relationship that cost buys no period at all and would raise the product outright. They stay exactly as the baseline has them.
  • The my_fir tap products not individually converted: none — all 41 listed my_fir ids are covered. Note that the f2 and h2 id lists enumerate 5 regions each while the source has 7 taps; the rewrite covers all seven taps in those modules regardless of how detection grouped them.

Why this lowers the product and what the risks are. Area ≈ 8.46e7 − 1.07e7 (42 tiles) + ~6e6 (the new T/U/Z flip-flops and two 17-bit pre-adders per instance, net ≈ +52 BLEs per FIR after dropping n_delay_reg6 and one 28-bit adder level) ≈ 8.0e7, i.e. about −5% on area, with period ~8.0 ns instead of 9.14 ns, i.e. about −12%: product ≈ 6.4e8 against the kept 7.73e8 (−46% against the 1.18888e9 baseline). Risks, in order: (1) the fltr_compute d_out_tmp stage (seven 20-bit values through a three-level soft adder tree) is untouched and may itself sit near 7.5-8 ns, which would floor the period and cap the delay gain — that is also why I am not spending extra tiles to push my_fir any lower; (2) my wire estimates use the table medians, and the trailing wire-plus-LUT into the dout flip-flop measured 2.59 ns in the last run, which I have carried into the 8.0 ns figure but which routing could worsen; (3) if the period does not improve at all, the tile reduction alone still gives ≈ 8.0e7 × 9.14 ns ≈ 7.3e8, below the kept 7.73e8, so the change is downside-protected; (4) the main correctness risk is index alignment on T, U and Z — each must be written under new_data_rdy and must use exactly n_delay_reg4, n_delay_reg2 and the k-sets above, since a one-cycle slip there silently changes the filter. No new operation or datatype family is introduced: only the existing unsigned adds, the existing constant multiplies, and additional registers of the same kind already in the module.

PLAN:

What changes. Each my_fir_* is re-associated into three pipeline stages that reproduce the same transfer function with the same latency. Writing d(τ) for din at enabled cycle τ (all registers advance only on new_data_rdy, so τ counts enabled cycles), the baseline computes dout(τ+1) = Σ_k d(τ-k)·C_k. Every coefficient set here is symmetric (C6=C0, C5=C1, C4=C2), and the f3/h1/h3/h4 sets drop the centre tap (C3=0, its product is already absent from the source), so:

  • T <= din + n_delay_reg4 gives T(τ) = d(τ-1)+d(τ-5), the taps that share C1=C5.
  • U <= din + n_delay_reg2 gives U(τ-1) = d(τ-2)+d(τ-4), the taps that share C2=C4, evaluated one cycle earlier where Z is built.
  • Z <= U*C2 + n_delay_reg2*C3 + n_delay_reg5*C0 (7-tap) or Z <= U*C2 + n_delay_reg5*C0 (6-tap), so Z(τ) carries exactly the k=2,3,4,6 (resp. k=2,4,6) terms of the sum due at τ.
  • dout <= din*C0 + T*C1 + Z supplies k=0,1,5 and the carried partial.

Summing these gives Σ_{k} d(τ-k)·C_k term for term; only the association order changes, which is exact because every operand and coefficient is non-negative and nothing is truncated before the final 28-bit assignment (largest coefficient sum is 673 for f2/h2, 673·65535 = 4.4e7 < 2^28, so no partial sum and no block result exceeds 28 bits and result[27:0] is the exact value). n_delay_reg6 becomes dead and is deleted; n_delay_reg1..5 keep the shift chain. T, U and Z are written under the same new_data_rdy enable as everything else, so the enable and hold behaviour is unchanged, and with power-up zeros the startup transient matches the baseline's as well.

Live inputs/outputs preserved. The module ports are untouched: dout is still a 28-bit register written one enabled cycle after the sample it summarizes, and output_data_ready is unchanged, so the top-level capture if (my_fir_rdy_x) vidin_out_reg_x <= vidin_out_temp_x (lines 525-540) and everything downstream in steer_fltr see identical values at identical cycles. T, U, Z are new internal registers with no other readers; nothing that leaves the module is taken inside a block. No register that anything depends on is deleted except n_delay_reg6, which has no reader after the rewrite.

Numbers I am committing to. 102 blocks (3 each in f1/f2/h2, 2 each in f3/h1/h3/h4 → 17 per instance group × 6 instances), down from the 144 blocks of the kept rewrite. Blocks take a tile alone, so DSP tiles go 200 → 158, i.e. 61 fewer than the unmodified design's 219 and 42 fewer than the kept rewrite, worth −1.07e7 min-width transistor areas. The longest series of blocks in any stage is one: every stage is register → one block → at most one soft adder → register, so no block-to-block routing hop exists anywhere. Worst stage from the table: clock-to-Q 0.06 + register-to-block wire 1.31 + block 2.14 + block-into-soft wire 1.38 + one 28-bit carry chain ≈ 0.5 + the trailing wire/LUT into the flip-flop seen in the measured report (2.43 + 0.15) + setup 0.02 ≈ 8.0 ns; without that trailing LUT it is ≈ 7.7 ns. The T/U pre-add stages are register → 17-bit add → register ≈ 4.1 ns, and the 6-tap Z stage is register → block → register ≈ 5.8 ns, both well clear.

What leaves the slowest stage. The kept rewrite's critical stage is one block followed by two soft adder levels ($add~572 then the 21-bit $add~573) and then the LUT into $dffe~580. This rewrite removes one of those two levels — the 1.00 ns inter-adder wire plus its ~0.49 ns carry chain — by cutting each FIR's stage down to a single block plus a single 28-bit add, which is possible because the folded pair sums (T, U) and the older taps (Z) arrive already registered rather than being built combinationally in the same stage. Yes, this is the slowest stage: every remaining my_fir instance has the same shape, and all 42 are rewritten identically, so none is left behind to hold the period at 9.14 ns.

Candidates left, with reasons.

  • All 42 fltr_compute_ multiply candidates (lines 859-865, 890-894, 928-934, 959-965, 993-997, 1030-1036, 1065-1071), left:* these seven 8-bit × ≤9-bit products per instance do feed a common reduction (d_out_tmp), so they would be legal to fuse, but they currently pack four to a tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt on 54 tiles. Fusing them into comb_sop_2_18 would need ~4 blocks per instance × 42 = 168 tiles that each block holds alone, i.e. +114 tiles ≈ +2.9e7 area, and their stage is not the slowest one, so by the slowest-stage/area relationship that cost buys no period at all and would raise the product outright. They stay exactly as the baseline has them.
  • The my_fir tap products not individually converted: none — all 41 listed my_fir ids are covered. Note that the f2 and h2 id lists enumerate 5 regions each while the source has 7 taps; the rewrite covers all seven taps in those modules regardless of how detection grouped them.

Why this lowers the product and what the risks are. Area ≈ 8.46e7 − 1.07e7 (42 tiles) + ~6e6 (the new T/U/Z flip-flops and two 17-bit pre-adders per instance, net ≈ +52 BLEs per FIR after dropping n_delay_reg6 and one 28-bit adder level) ≈ 8.0e7, i.e. about −5% on area, with period ~8.0 ns instead of 9.14 ns, i.e. about −12%: product ≈ 6.4e8 against the kept 7.73e8 (−46% against the 1.18888e9 baseline). Risks, in order: (1) the fltr_compute d_out_tmp stage (seven 20-bit values through a three-level soft adder tree) is untouched and may itself sit near 7.5-8 ns, which would floor the period and cap the delay gain — that is also why I am not spending extra tiles to push my_fir any lower; (2) my wire estimates use the table medians, and the trailing wire-plus-LUT into the dout flip-flop measured 2.59 ns in the last run, which I have carried into the 8.0 ns figure but which routing could worsen; (3) if the period does not improve at all, the tile reduction alone still gives ≈ 8.0e7 × 9.14 ns ≈ 7.3e8, below the kept 7.73e8, so the change is downside-protected; (4) the main correctness risk is index alignment on T, U and Z — each must be written under new_data_rdy and must use exactly n_delay_reg4, n_delay_reg2 and the k-sets above, since a one-cycle slip there silently changes the filter. No new operation or datatype family is introduced: only the existing unsigned adds, the existing constant multiplies, and additional registers of the same kind already in the module.

  • (a) Function preserved. Coefficients confirmed all non-negative and symmetric as the plan states (stereovision2.v:1440-1449 f1 = 29,101,15,235,15,101,29; f2/h2 = 4,42,163,255,163,42,4; f3 = 12,77,148,0,148,77,12; h1 = 15,25,193,0,193,25,15; h3/h4 = 9,56,109,0,109,56,9). Index check on the folding: with n_delay_regK = d(τ−K) at cycle τ, T written at τ−1 = d(τ−1)+d(τ−5) → covers k=1,5 (C5=C1); U written at τ−2 → d(τ−2)+d(τ−4) → k=2,4 (C4=C2); Z written at τ−1 reads n_delay_reg2=d(τ−3) (k=3, 7-tap only) and n_delay_reg5=d(τ−6) (k=6, C6=C0); final stage adds din*C0. Sum reproduces Σ d(τ−k)·C_k exactly, written at the same enabled cycle, under the same new_data_rdy enable. All operands unsigned, max magnitude 673·65535 ≈ 4.4e7 < 2²⁸, so no truncation difference against the baseline's 28-bit dout. n_delay_reg6 is read nowhere else (stereovision2.v:1483,1492 etc.), so its deletion is safe; n_delay_reg3 is retained for the shift chain.
  • (b) Only existing unsigned constant-multiplies, unsigned adds, and additional registers of the same kind. No new op/datatype family.
  • (c) Every product in the mapping traces to a real tap of the same dout reduction; T/U folding merges two existing equal-coefficient products rather than inventing terms. Covering the f2/h2 k=0 and k=6 taps that the region list omits is within the same reduction statement and does not fabricate products.
  • (d) No mode island: every block is driven by live registers (din, T, U, n_delay_reg2/5) and its result flows into Z → dout → vidin_out_reg_* (stereovision2.v:514-545). The one zero-tied operand slot on B2 of the 7-tap modules is an idle second term on a block whose first term and output are live, not a constant-driven or dead block. Ports dout/output_data_ready and downstream steer_fltr timing are unchanged.

Instance count checks out (6 h_fltr instances at stereovision2.v:188-197, one of each my_fir_* inside at 514-520), so 17 blocks/instance × 6 = 102 is self-consistent. Timing/area figures are estimates and, per the review rule, are not grounds for revision.

PLAN:

What changes. Each my_fir_* is re-associated into three pipeline stages that reproduce the same transfer function with the same latency. Writing d(τ) for din at enabled cycle τ (all registers advance only on new_data_rdy, so τ counts enabled cycles), the baseline computes dout(τ+1) = Σ_k d(τ-k)·C_k. Every coefficient set here is symmetric (C6=C0, C5=C1, C4=C2), and the f3/h1/h3/h4 sets drop the centre tap (C3=0, its product is already absent from the source), so:

  • T <= din + n_delay_reg4 gives T(τ) = d(τ-1)+d(τ-5), the taps that share C1=C5.
  • U <= din + n_delay_reg2 gives U(τ-1) = d(τ-2)+d(τ-4), the taps that share C2=C4, evaluated one cycle earlier where Z is built.
  • Z <= U*C2 + n_delay_reg2*C3 + n_delay_reg5*C0 (7-tap) or Z <= U*C2 + n_delay_reg5*C0 (6-tap), so Z(τ) carries exactly the k=2,3,4,6 (resp. k=2,4,6) terms of the sum due at τ.
  • dout <= din*C0 + T*C1 + Z supplies k=0,1,5 and the carried partial.

Summing these gives Σ_{k} d(τ-k)·C_k term for term; only the association order changes, which is exact because every operand and coefficient is non-negative and nothing is truncated before the final 28-bit assignment (largest coefficient sum is 673 for f2/h2, 673·65535 = 4.4e7 < 2^28, so no partial sum and no block result exceeds 28 bits and result[27:0] is the exact value). n_delay_reg6 becomes dead and is deleted; n_delay_reg1..5 keep the shift chain. T, U and Z are written under the same new_data_rdy enable as everything else, so the enable and hold behaviour is unchanged, and with power-up zeros the startup transient matches the baseline's as well.

Live inputs/outputs preserved. The module ports are untouched: dout is still a 28-bit register written one enabled cycle after the sample it summarizes, and output_data_ready is unchanged, so the top-level capture if (my_fir_rdy_x) vidin_out_reg_x <= vidin_out_temp_x (lines 525-540) and everything downstream in steer_fltr see identical values at identical cycles. T, U, Z are new internal registers with no other readers; nothing that leaves the module is taken inside a block. No register that anything depends on is deleted except n_delay_reg6, which has no reader after the rewrite.

Numbers I am committing to. 102 blocks (3 each in f1/f2/h2, 2 each in f3/h1/h3/h4 → 17 per instance group × 6 instances), down from the 144 blocks of the kept rewrite. Blocks take a tile alone, so DSP tiles go 200 → 158, i.e. 61 fewer than the unmodified design's 219 and 42 fewer than the kept rewrite, worth −1.07e7 min-width transistor areas. The longest series of blocks in any stage is one: every stage is register → one block → at most one soft adder → register, so no block-to-block routing hop exists anywhere. Worst stage from the table: clock-to-Q 0.06 + register-to-block wire 1.31 + block 2.14 + block-into-soft wire 1.38 + one 28-bit carry chain ≈ 0.5 + the trailing wire/LUT into the flip-flop seen in the measured report (2.43 + 0.15) + setup 0.02 ≈ 8.0 ns; without that trailing LUT it is ≈ 7.7 ns. The T/U pre-add stages are register → 17-bit add → register ≈ 4.1 ns, and the 6-tap Z stage is register → block → register ≈ 5.8 ns, both well clear.

What leaves the slowest stage. The kept rewrite's critical stage is one block followed by two soft adder levels ($add~572 then the 21-bit $add~573) and then the LUT into $dffe~580. This rewrite removes one of those two levels — the 1.00 ns inter-adder wire plus its ~0.49 ns carry chain — by cutting each FIR's stage down to a single block plus a single 28-bit add, which is possible because the folded pair sums (T, U) and the older taps (Z) arrive already registered rather than being built combinationally in the same stage. Yes, this is the slowest stage: every remaining my_fir instance has the same shape, and all 42 are rewritten identically, so none is left behind to hold the period at 9.14 ns.

Candidates left, with reasons.

  • All 42 fltr_compute_ multiply candidates (lines 859-865, 890-894, 928-934, 959-965, 993-997, 1030-1036, 1065-1071), left:* these seven 8-bit × ≤9-bit products per instance do feed a common reduction (d_out_tmp), so they would be legal to fuse, but they currently pack four to a tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt on 54 tiles. Fusing them into comb_sop_2_18 would need ~4 blocks per instance × 42 = 168 tiles that each block holds alone, i.e. +114 tiles ≈ +2.9e7 area, and their stage is not the slowest one, so by the slowest-stage/area relationship that cost buys no period at all and would raise the product outright. They stay exactly as the baseline has them.
  • The my_fir tap products not individually converted: none — all 41 listed my_fir ids are covered. Note that the f2 and h2 id lists enumerate 5 regions each while the source has 7 taps; the rewrite covers all seven taps in those modules regardless of how detection grouped them.

Why this lowers the product and what the risks are. Area ≈ 8.46e7 − 1.07e7 (42 tiles) + ~6e6 (the new T/U/Z flip-flops and two 17-bit pre-adders per instance, net ≈ +52 BLEs per FIR after dropping n_delay_reg6 and one 28-bit adder level) ≈ 8.0e7, i.e. about −5% on area, with period ~8.0 ns instead of 9.14 ns, i.e. about −12%: product ≈ 6.4e8 against the kept 7.73e8 (−46% against the 1.18888e9 baseline). Risks, in order: (1) the fltr_compute d_out_tmp stage (seven 20-bit values through a three-level soft adder tree) is untouched and may itself sit near 7.5-8 ns, which would floor the period and cap the delay gain — that is also why I am not spending extra tiles to push my_fir any lower; (2) my wire estimates use the table medians, and the trailing wire-plus-LUT into the dout flip-flop measured 2.59 ns in the last run, which I have carried into the 8.0 ns figure but which routing could worsen; (3) if the period does not improve at all, the tile reduction alone still gives ≈ 8.0e7 × 9.14 ns ≈ 7.3e8, below the kept 7.73e8, so the change is downside-protected; (4) the main correctness risk is index alignment on T, U and Z — each must be written under new_data_rdy and must use exactly n_delay_reg4, n_delay_reg2 and the k-sets above, since a one-cycle slip there silently changes the filter. No new operation or datatype family is introduced: only the existing unsigned adds, the existing constant multiplies, and additional registers of the same kind already in the module.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: syntax + elaboration + cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Runs plain yosys (read_verilog; hierarchy; proc; opt; stat) on the one file: no arch, no
# parmys, no hard-block library. Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole
# design (the last "Number of cells" table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub,
# registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated
# module by name, which is where a hard-block instantiation such as comb_mult_add_16 shows up
# with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
out="$(yosys -p "read_verilog $f; hierarchy -auto-top; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

module my_fir_f1 (clk, new_data_rdy, output_data_ready, din, dout);

//coefdata=29,101,-15,-235,-15,101,29;

	//parameter `WIDTH = 5'b10000;

    input clk; 
    input[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] din; 
    output[28 - 1:0] dout; 
    reg[28 - 1:0] dout;
	input new_data_rdy;
	output output_data_ready;
	reg output_data_ready;

    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg1;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg2;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg3;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg4;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg5;

    // folded taps: T = k1+k5, U = k2+k4 (symmetric coefficients), Z = carried partial sum
    reg[16:0] T;
    reg[16:0] U;
    reg[28 - 1:0] Z;

    wire[18:0] coef0 = `COEF0_b;
    wire[18:0] coef1 = `COEF1_b;
    wire[18:0] coef2 = `COEF2_b;
    wire[18:0] coef3 = `COEF3_b;

    wire[63:0] sop_z_hi;
    wire[63:0] sop_z_lo;
    wire[63:0] sop_dout;

    comb_sop_2_18 sop_z_hi_inst (
        .ax({1'b0, U}), .ay(coef2),
        .bx({2'b0, n_delay_reg2}), .by(coef3),
        .result(sop_z_hi));

    comb_sop_2_18 sop_z_lo_inst (
        .ax({2'b0, n_delay_reg5}), .ay(coef0),
        .bx(18'd0), .by(19'd0),
        .result(sop_z_lo));

    comb_sop_2_18 sop_dout_inst (
        .ax({2'b0, din}), .ay(coef0),
        .bx({1'b0, T}), .by(coef1),
        .result(sop_dout));

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
		if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1)
		begin
			n_delay_reg1 <= din;
			n_delay_reg2 <= n_delay_reg1;
			n_delay_reg3 <= n_delay_reg2;
			n_delay_reg4 <= n_delay_reg3;
			n_delay_reg5 <= n_delay_reg4;

			T <= din + n_delay_reg4;
			U <= din + n_delay_reg2;
			Z <= sop_z_hi[28 - 1:0] + sop_z_lo[28 - 1:0];
		
			output_data_ready <= 1'b1;
			dout <= sop_dout[28 - 1:0] + Z;
		end
		else
		begin
			output_data_ready <= 1'b0;
		end
	end
endmodule

After the edit every instance is still exactly that: a 7-tap FIR tap-weight sum-of-products registered into dout, driving output_data_ready/dout on the same new_data_rdy gate. No control-path or unrelated arithmetic was recruited.

Real region mapped, no fabricated terms (a). Each comb_sop_2_18 fuses two products that were literally adjacent terms of the same dout reduction:

  • sop_dout: din*C0 + T*C1, where T = din + n_delay_reg4 is the folded pair x[n‑1]+x[n‑5] (C1 = C5 in every filter).
  • sop_z_hi: U*C2 + n_delay_reg2*C3, with U = din + n_delay_reg2 = x[n‑2]+x[n‑4] (C2 = C4).
  • sop_z_lo / sop_z: the surviving C0*x[n‑6] term (C0 = C6), reached by retiming through Z instead of n_delay_reg6.

The pre-adders are the textbook symmetric fold, and the symmetry is real in the active defines for all seven filters (b: 29,101,15,235,15,101,29; c/2: 4,42,163,255,163,42,4; d: 12,77,148,0,148,77,12; 1: 15,25,193,0,193,25,15; 3/4: 9,56,109,0,109,56,9 — lines 1440–1930). Tracing the nonblocking semantics, dout at cycle n = C0·x[n] + C1·(x[n‑1]+x[n‑5]) + C2·(x[n‑2]+x[n‑4]) + C3·x[n‑3] + C0·x[n‑6] — bit-exact to the original expression at unchanged latency, since T,U,Z update under the same new_data_rdy gate. Widths hold: WIDTH_5B=16, T/U 17 b into 18 b ax/bx, coefficients ≤255 into 19 b ay/by, and max |Σ| (65535×673 ≈ 4.4e7) fits the 28-bit Z/dout truncation with no overflow. The bx(18'd0)/by(19'd0) half of sop_z_lo is odd-arity slack (5 folded products into 2-term blocks), not a manufactured term.

Not a mode island (b). dout → vidin_out_temp_* (stereovision2.v:514–520) → vidin_out_reg_* (:527–553) → steer_fltr (:521) → real_z/imag_z/real_p/imag_p, the design's real outputs. The mode result is the only source of dout; nothing is parked on a sink.

Not a variant (d). T2, manifest introduces no operations or datatypes; datatype and consumer set match the witness exactly. No sibling-evidence axis is required or claimed.

Noted but non-disqualifying: the partial fold (C0 pair handled by the Z retiming rather than a third pre-adder) costs one extra multiply versus a full fold, and the f3/h1/h3/h4 header comments describe antisymmetric coefficient sets whose negative values are commented out — if those were re-enabled the pre-adders would need to become subtractors. Against the source as actually compiled, the transformation is exact.

Baseline: the unmodified stereovision2 under this run's VPR settings (regime 'koios_medium': channel width 300, device koios_medium, seed 1) has a critical path of 12.4624 ns and uses 219 DSP tiles of the device's 770, one block per tile. Its used logic-block area is 9.53973e+07 minimum-width transistor areas (one DSP tile 253779, one cluster 27905), so its area-delay product is 1.18888e+09. Its slowest stage is in my_fir: one hard multiply on a DSP tile (two_mult_18x19), then six adder levels with their carry chains, then one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop. The next slowest stage, in a different my_fir instance (endpoint group $dffe~788, not path 1's $dffe~456), is the same shape as path 1 — one hard multiply on a DSP tile, six adder levels with their carry chains, one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop, 12.297 ns, so shortening the slowest stage past that point buys nothing on its own. Any path your rewrite creates is compared against that critical path.

Rewrite rules

A stage is the logic between one register and the next. A block is one instance of the target mode. These rules hold for any synchronous design on any FPGA. Numbers that depend on this architecture are in the last section; use them, do not restate them as rules.

Must hold

Going against these produces a wrong design, not a slower one.

Observability. Only a block's output is visible. A value read by anything other than the arithmetic being taken into the block (another expression, a module output port, another module) cannot go inside a block. Keep it outside, or recompute it for those readers. Check the source; detection does not see port consumers. Operands are exempt: the block takes a copy and the original signal still exists.

Register control. A register carries its reset, enable and initial value. These modes hold no registers, so taking a register inside deletes that behaviour. If anything depends on it, keep the register and drive it from the block's result, or leave the site alone.

Arithmetic. The block computes the mode's expression on signed ports. Match the original bit for bit or leave the site alone.

design operandon a signed portallowed
unsigned, narrower than the portzero-extendyes
unsigned, as wide as the port, range provably below the signed maximum (constant coefficient, bounded value)zero-extend, state the bound and where it comes fromyes
unsigned, as wide as the port, range not boundable from the source (a top-level input)no exact representationno
original truncates each product before the suma fused sum truncated after differsno
original's narrow sum register wrapsthe low bits of the wider result reproduce the wrapyes
Weigh

The clock period is the delay of the slowest stage in the whole design. A stage's delay is the sum of everything on it: each block's fixed delay, each wire, each soft cell. Each relationship below names what it does to delay and to area. If a plan goes against one, say why.

1. Slowest stage → all outputs

Your task names the design's slowest stage and what is on it.

Slowest stage → delay

Relationship: A rewrite that does not touch the slowest stage cannot make the design faster, and must leave every stage no slower than it was. A rewrite that does touch it must make it shorter, not merely different. Compare every stage you change against it.

Slowest stage → area

Relationship: A rewrite that cannot shorten the clock period is paid for in tiles alone. Say so in the plan.

2. Block to register → delay

Relationship: A block's result goes to a register, or into the next block, with nothing but wire between. Any soft arithmetic between a block and its register is added to the stage.

3. Blocks in series → all outputs
Blocks in series → delay

Relationship: Each block in series adds its own delay plus one wire. Sum them with the wire in and the wire out, and compare against the slowest stage. That comparison, not a fixed count, says how many fit.

Blocks in series → area

Relationship: None. Series or side by side, the same blocks take the same tiles.

4. Arithmetic inside the block → all outputs

Arithmetic inside the block is what the mode's expression computes rather than what sits in series with it: a multiply and one addend, or two products and their sum, depending on the mode.

Arithmetic inside the block → delay

Relationship: Free. The block's delay is the mode's own and does not rise because its adder is used. This is where a conversion wins: soft logic leaves the stage and the block's delay already covers the work. An adder feeding the block's addend port is mapped into the block; an adder reading the block's result is on the path after it (rule 2). A block whose addend port is tied to a constant takes in nothing; if the multiply it replaces is already on a tile, the conversion changes the tile count and nothing else.

Arithmetic inside the block → area

Relationship: Flip-flops fall where product registers go. Do not count on LUT savings.

5. Registers → all outputs
Registers → delay

Relationship: A register may move only if no stage becomes longer and the module's latency is unchanged. If one must be added to keep latency, put it where it splits the longest stage. Every other operand entering that stage must be delayed by the same amount, or the stage adds values from different cycles.

Registers → area

Relationship: A register placed mid-chain costs operand-delay registers that a register after the chain does not.

6. Tiles → area

Relationship: A block occupies one DSP tile in one mode. Do not assume the multiply it replaces frees a tile: the synthesis tool may already have placed that multiply on a tile shared with others. Count the blocks against the tiles the unmodified design uses and the device's count, both in your task.

Every DSP mode costs the same 2.14 ns. The invented modes have no chain ports, so a partial sum passes between blocks through general routing. The packer can place up to four multiplies of 9 bits or less on one tile and up to two of 18 bits or less; a block in either invented mode takes its tile alone.

PLAN:

What changes. Each my_fir_* is a symmetric FIR over a tap delay line, so the taps that share a coefficient are pre-added once and multiplied once: din*c0 + n_delay_reg6*c0 becomes (din+n_delay_reg6)*c0, and likewise for the c1 and c2 pairs. That turns 7 (or 6) products per instance into 4 (or 3), which is 2 blocks per 7-tap instance and 1 block + 1 ordinary multiply per 6-tap instance. The products of each instance already feed one common reduction — the single registered 28-bit dout sum — which is what the mode requires; nothing is fused across instances.

Exactness. Every operand is unsigned: din and the delay regs are 16-bit, so each pre-sum is at most 65535+65535 = 131070, which fits a 17-bit value and therefore a zero-extended 18-bit signed ax/bx port (signed max 131071). Coefficients are the COEF* defines, all ≤ 255, on a 19-bit signed port. The baseline evaluates the whole tap sum in a 32-bit self-determined context with no per-product truncation and only then truncates to dout[27:0]; the largest possible full sum is 65535 × (sum of coefficients ≤ 673) ≈ 4.4e7 < 2^28, so no wrap occurs and the low 28 bits of the fused result are bit-identical. Distributing the shared coefficient over the tap pair is exact in full precision, so the folded form equals the original term-by-term sum.

Live inputs/outputs and consumers. din, new_data_rdy, output_data_ready and dout keep their ports and meaning. n_delay_reg1..6 keep their registers, their shift order and the if (new_data_rdy) enable — the pre-sums are combinational reads of those registers, so nothing that carried an enable is absorbed into a block. dout stays an enabled register driven by the final soft add, and output_data_ready is untouched, so module latency is unchanged. The delay-line registers are read only inside their own module, and the block takes copies of them as operands, so observability is preserved. No new operation family or datatype is introduced: only adds, multiplies and the target block.

Budget. 60 blocks, each alone on a tile; the 24 leftover folded multiplies (24 module instances of f3/h1/h3/h4) are 17×8, so two pack per tile in 18x19 mode → 12 tiles; the 56 tiles the rest of the design uses (chiefly the fltr_compute_* 9x9 multiplies, four to a tile) are untouched. 128 tiles total, 91 fewer than the unmodified design's 219 and 30 fewer than the kept revision's 158, well inside the device's 770. No two blocks are in series anywhere: the longest block series in any stage is 1, so the stage is clk-to-Q 0.06 + wire to the pre-adder + one 17-bit soft adder level + wire into the block + 2.14 + wire out + one 28-bit soft adder level + setup ≈ 7.6 ns, versus the baseline critical path of 12.4624 ns.

Effect on the slowest stage. The slowest stage is not in my_fir: the kept revision's measured path is latch → $mul~896 (9x9, fltr_compute) → latch, 7.62 ns of which 4.7 ns is wire and 2.14 ns is the block itself. That stage is a bare register-to-register multiply and cannot be shortened by this mode — a comb_sop block has the same 2.14 ns delay and the same routing, so the period stays where it is. This rewrite is therefore paid for, and pays back, in tiles: it removes six adder levels and a LUT per my_fir stage (baseline shape) and keeps the same two soft levels as the kept revision — one moved ahead of the block, one after it — while halving the multiplies that need silicon. Area falls by roughly 30 DSP tiles (≈7.6e6) against an added ≈126 17-bit pre-adders and three fewer post-adders per instance set (≈+2.5e6 net soft), so the expected used area is ≈7.1e7 and the expected product ≈5.4e8, below the kept 5.82e8.

Left alone, with reasons.

  • All 42 fltr_compute_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 multiply candidates (ids at lines 859–865, 890–894, 928–934, 959–965, 993–997, 1030–1036, 1065–1071): three separate reasons, any one of which is disqualifying. (1) Delay: these sit on the design's slowest stage, q_i <= din_slice * const between two registers; replacing them with blocks leaves the identical 2.14 ns block plus identical routing, so the stage gets no shorter — rule "a rewrite that touches the slowest stage must make it shorter, not merely different". (2) Area: the packer already puts four of these 9x9 multiplies on one tile, while a comb_sop block holds only two products and takes its tile alone, so conversion would roughly double that region's tiles for no delay gain. (3) Exactness, for fltr_compute_f1 q4 (coefficient 277), f3 q3/q5 (364) and h4 q4 (324): the product is truncated into the 17-bit q register and then sign-extended from q[16] into the 20-bit sum, so those products wrap negative for large din; a fused full-precision sum would differ, which the arithmetic table forbids. The remaining fltr_compute coefficients (all ≤ 257) would fuse exactly, but reasons (1) and (2) still rule them out.
  • Also not converted into blocks, though restructured by the same fold: my_fir_f3 1604$187/1605$189, my_fir_h1 1663$200/1664$202, my_fir_h3 1777$228/1778$230, my_fir_h4 1835$241/1836$243. These are the third folded product in a 6-tap instance; a block holds two products, and giving a lone product a block would cost a whole tile for a half-used block, whereas an ordinary 17×8 multiply shares a tile with a second one (0.5 tile) at the identical 2.14 ns. They still feed the same dout reduction through the same single post-adder.

Risks. (1) The pre-adder now sits between the tap registers and the block; if the placer stretches the adder-to-DSP wire, the my_fir stage could pass the 7.62 ns fltr_compute path and become critical at ~8 ns, which would make the product roughly neutral rather than better — the 30-tile drop in DSP occupancy works the other way and should shorten routing. (2) Tile count assumes the packer pairs the 24 leftover 17×8 multiplies two to a tile; if it gives each its own tile the design lands at 140 tiles, which is still 18 below the kept revision. (3) (din+n_delay_reg6) at 131070 is one below the 18-bit signed port maximum, so the widening must be a plain zero-extension of a 17-bit sum, not a re-slice to 16 bits.

PLAN:

What changes. Each my_fir_* is a symmetric FIR over a tap delay line, so the taps that share a coefficient are pre-added once and multiplied once: din*c0 + n_delay_reg6*c0 becomes (din+n_delay_reg6)*c0, and likewise for the c1 and c2 pairs. That turns 7 (or 6) products per instance into 4 (or 3), which is 2 blocks per 7-tap instance and 1 block + 1 ordinary multiply per 6-tap instance. The products of each instance already feed one common reduction — the single registered 28-bit dout sum — which is what the mode requires; nothing is fused across instances.

Exactness. Every operand is unsigned: din and the delay regs are 16-bit, so each pre-sum is at most 65535+65535 = 131070, which fits a 17-bit value and therefore a zero-extended 18-bit signed ax/bx port (signed max 131071). Coefficients are the COEF* defines, all ≤ 255, on a 19-bit signed port. The baseline evaluates the whole tap sum in a 32-bit self-determined context with no per-product truncation and only then truncates to dout[27:0]; the largest possible full sum is 65535 × (sum of coefficients ≤ 673) ≈ 4.4e7 < 2^28, so no wrap occurs and the low 28 bits of the fused result are bit-identical. Distributing the shared coefficient over the tap pair is exact in full precision, so the folded form equals the original term-by-term sum.

Live inputs/outputs and consumers. din, new_data_rdy, output_data_ready and dout keep their ports and meaning. n_delay_reg1..6 keep their registers, their shift order and the if (new_data_rdy) enable — the pre-sums are combinational reads of those registers, so nothing that carried an enable is absorbed into a block. dout stays an enabled register driven by the final soft add, and output_data_ready is untouched, so module latency is unchanged. The delay-line registers are read only inside their own module, and the block takes copies of them as operands, so observability is preserved. No new operation family or datatype is introduced: only adds, multiplies and the target block.

Budget. 60 blocks, each alone on a tile; the 24 leftover folded multiplies (24 module instances of f3/h1/h3/h4) are 17×8, so two pack per tile in 18x19 mode → 12 tiles; the 56 tiles the rest of the design uses (chiefly the fltr_compute_* 9x9 multiplies, four to a tile) are untouched. 128 tiles total, 91 fewer than the unmodified design's 219 and 30 fewer than the kept revision's 158, well inside the device's 770. No two blocks are in series anywhere: the longest block series in any stage is 1, so the stage is clk-to-Q 0.06 + wire to the pre-adder + one 17-bit soft adder level + wire into the block + 2.14 + wire out + one 28-bit soft adder level + setup ≈ 7.6 ns, versus the baseline critical path of 12.4624 ns.

Effect on the slowest stage. The slowest stage is not in my_fir: the kept revision's measured path is latch → $mul~896 (9x9, fltr_compute) → latch, 7.62 ns of which 4.7 ns is wire and 2.14 ns is the block itself. That stage is a bare register-to-register multiply and cannot be shortened by this mode — a comb_sop block has the same 2.14 ns delay and the same routing, so the period stays where it is. This rewrite is therefore paid for, and pays back, in tiles: it removes six adder levels and a LUT per my_fir stage (baseline shape) and keeps the same two soft levels as the kept revision — one moved ahead of the block, one after it — while halving the multiplies that need silicon. Area falls by roughly 30 DSP tiles (≈7.6e6) against an added ≈126 17-bit pre-adders and three fewer post-adders per instance set (≈+2.5e6 net soft), so the expected used area is ≈7.1e7 and the expected product ≈5.4e8, below the kept 5.82e8.

Left alone, with reasons.

  • All 42 fltr_compute_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 multiply candidates (ids at lines 859–865, 890–894, 928–934, 959–965, 993–997, 1030–1036, 1065–1071): three separate reasons, any one of which is disqualifying. (1) Delay: these sit on the design's slowest stage, q_i <= din_slice * const between two registers; replacing them with blocks leaves the identical 2.14 ns block plus identical routing, so the stage gets no shorter — rule "a rewrite that touches the slowest stage must make it shorter, not merely different". (2) Area: the packer already puts four of these 9x9 multiplies on one tile, while a comb_sop block holds only two products and takes its tile alone, so conversion would roughly double that region's tiles for no delay gain. (3) Exactness, for fltr_compute_f1 q4 (coefficient 277), f3 q3/q5 (364) and h4 q4 (324): the product is truncated into the 17-bit q register and then sign-extended from q[16] into the 20-bit sum, so those products wrap negative for large din; a fused full-precision sum would differ, which the arithmetic table forbids. The remaining fltr_compute coefficients (all ≤ 257) would fuse exactly, but reasons (1) and (2) still rule them out.
  • Also not converted into blocks, though restructured by the same fold: my_fir_f3 1604$187/1605$189, my_fir_h1 1663$200/1664$202, my_fir_h3 1777$228/1778$230, my_fir_h4 1835$241/1836$243. These are the third folded product in a 6-tap instance; a block holds two products, and giving a lone product a block would cost a whole tile for a half-used block, whereas an ordinary 17×8 multiply shares a tile with a second one (0.5 tile) at the identical 2.14 ns. They still feed the same dout reduction through the same single post-adder.

Risks. (1) The pre-adder now sits between the tap registers and the block; if the placer stretches the adder-to-DSP wire, the my_fir stage could pass the 7.62 ns fltr_compute path and become critical at ~8 ns, which would make the product roughly neutral rather than better — the 30-tile drop in DSP occupancy works the other way and should shorten routing. (2) Tile count assumes the packer pairs the 24 leftover 17×8 multiplies two to a tile; if it gives each its own tile the design lands at 140 tiles, which is still 18 below the kept revision. (3) (din+n_delay_reg6) at 131070 is one below the 18-bit signed port maximum, so the widening must be a plain zero-extension of a 17-bit sum, not a re-slice to 16 bits.

Read these files in this directory: stereovision2.v

response

I'll verify the plan against the source.

APPROVE

Verified against /work/stereovision2.v:

  • (a) Function preserved. WIDTH_5B = 16, so din/n_delay_reg1..6 are 16-bit unsigned (stereovision2.v:1451, 1460, 1467-1472). Coefficient sets are genuinely symmetric with the pairings the plan uses — f1 29,101,15,235,15,101,29 (:1440-1449), f2/h2 4,42,163,255,163,42,4 (:1500-1506, :1675-1681), f3 12,77,148,0,148,77,12 (:1561-1567), h1 15,25,193,0,193,25,15 (:1616-1625), h3/h4 9,56,109,0,109,56,9 (:1734-1740, :1792-1798). Products are evaluated in a 32-bit self-determined context and only the final sum is truncated into dout[27:0] (:1486-1492 etc.), and the worst-case full sum is 65535×673 ≈ 4.41e7 < 2^28, so distributing the shared coefficient over each tap pair is bit-exact. Pre-sums max 131070, inside a zero-extended 17-bit value on an 18-bit signed port (131071), as the plan itself flags. Delay-line shift order, the new_data_rdy enable, output_data_ready, and the registered dout are all left intact, so latency and observability are unchanged.
  • (b) Only adds, multiplies, and the target comb_sop block; no new datatype (int32 throughout).
  • (c) No fabricated terms. Region count matches exactly: f1 7, f2 5, h2 5 (the ×4 taps are shifts, not $mul cells), f3/h1/h3/h4 4 each = 33. Every product placed in a block is a real tap term of that instance's single dout reduction; the f2/h2 s0*4 term exists in the RTL sum (:1542, :1548, :1716, :1722) and shares that same reduction, so absorbing it is folding, not invention. No block is half-filled with a tie-off.
  • (d) No mode island. dout → vidin_out_temp_* → vidin_out_reg_* → steer_fltr (:479-521), and the 6 h_fltr instances (:188-197) confirm the plan's 60-block / 24-leftover counts are consistent with the instance count.

Delay and area figures are estimates and the comparison against the "kept revision" path is unverifiable from the source alone, but neither is a listed violation.
