PLAN:

What changes. Each my_fir_* is a symmetric FIR over a tap delay line, so the taps that share a coefficient are pre-added once and multiplied once: din*c0 + n_delay_reg6*c0 becomes (din+n_delay_reg6)*c0, and likewise for the c1 and c2 pairs. That turns 7 (or 6) products per instance into 4 (or 3), which is 2 blocks per 7-tap instance and 1 block + 1 ordinary multiply per 6-tap instance. The products of each instance already feed one common reduction — the single registered 28-bit dout sum — which is what the mode requires; nothing is fused across instances.

Exactness. Every operand is unsigned: din and the delay regs are 16-bit, so each pre-sum is at most 65535+65535 = 131070, which fits a 17-bit value and therefore a zero-extended 18-bit signed ax/bx port (signed max 131071). Coefficients are the COEF* defines, all ≤ 255, on a 19-bit signed port. The baseline evaluates the whole tap sum in a 32-bit self-determined context with no per-product truncation and only then truncates to dout[27:0]; the largest possible full sum is 65535 × (sum of coefficients ≤ 673) ≈ 4.4e7 < 2^28, so no wrap occurs and the low 28 bits of the fused result are bit-identical. Distributing the shared coefficient over the tap pair is exact in full precision, so the folded form equals the original term-by-term sum.

Live inputs/outputs and consumers. din, new_data_rdy, output_data_ready and dout keep their ports and meaning. n_delay_reg1..6 keep their registers, their shift order and the if (new_data_rdy) enable — the pre-sums are combinational reads of those registers, so nothing that carried an enable is absorbed into a block. dout stays an enabled register driven by the final soft add, and output_data_ready is untouched, so module latency is unchanged. The delay-line registers are read only inside their own module, and the block takes copies of them as operands, so observability is preserved. No new operation family or datatype is introduced: only adds, multiplies and the target block.

Budget. 60 blocks, each alone on a tile; the 24 leftover folded multiplies (24 module instances of f3/h1/h3/h4) are 17×8, so two pack per tile in 18x19 mode → 12 tiles; the 56 tiles the rest of the design uses (chiefly the fltr_compute_* 9x9 multiplies, four to a tile) are untouched. 128 tiles total, 91 fewer than the unmodified design's 219 and 30 fewer than the kept revision's 158, well inside the device's 770. No two blocks are in series anywhere: the longest block series in any stage is 1, so the stage is clk-to-Q 0.06 + wire to the pre-adder + one 17-bit soft adder level + wire into the block + 2.14 + wire out + one 28-bit soft adder level + setup ≈ 7.6 ns, versus the baseline critical path of 12.4624 ns.

Effect on the slowest stage. The slowest stage is not in my_fir: the kept revision's measured path is latch → $mul~896 (9x9, fltr_compute) → latch, 7.62 ns of which 4.7 ns is wire and 2.14 ns is the block itself. That stage is a bare register-to-register multiply and cannot be shortened by this mode — a comb_sop block has the same 2.14 ns delay and the same routing, so the period stays where it is. This rewrite is therefore paid for, and pays back, in tiles: it removes six adder levels and a LUT per my_fir stage (baseline shape) and keeps the same two soft levels as the kept revision — one moved ahead of the block, one after it — while halving the multiplies that need silicon. Area falls by roughly 30 DSP tiles (≈7.6e6) against an added ≈126 17-bit pre-adders and three fewer post-adders per instance set (≈+2.5e6 net soft), so the expected used area is ≈7.1e7 and the expected product ≈5.4e8, below the kept 5.82e8.

Left alone, with reasons.

  • All 42 fltr_compute_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 multiply candidates (ids at lines 859–865, 890–894, 928–934, 959–965, 993–997, 1030–1036, 1065–1071): three separate reasons, any one of which is disqualifying. (1) Delay: these sit on the design's slowest stage, q_i <= din_slice * const between two registers; replacing them with blocks leaves the identical 2.14 ns block plus identical routing, so the stage gets no shorter — rule "a rewrite that touches the slowest stage must make it shorter, not merely different". (2) Area: the packer already puts four of these 9x9 multiplies on one tile, while a comb_sop block holds only two products and takes its tile alone, so conversion would roughly double that region's tiles for no delay gain. (3) Exactness, for fltr_compute_f1 q4 (coefficient 277), f3 q3/q5 (364) and h4 q4 (324): the product is truncated into the 17-bit q register and then sign-extended from q[16] into the 20-bit sum, so those products wrap negative for large din; a fused full-precision sum would differ, which the arithmetic table forbids. The remaining fltr_compute coefficients (all ≤ 257) would fuse exactly, but reasons (1) and (2) still rule them out.
  • Also not converted into blocks, though restructured by the same fold: my_fir_f3 1604$187/1605$189, my_fir_h1 1663$200/1664$202, my_fir_h3 1777$228/1778$230, my_fir_h4 1835$241/1836$243. These are the third folded product in a 6-tap instance; a block holds two products, and giving a lone product a block would cost a whole tile for a half-used block, whereas an ordinary 17×8 multiply shares a tile with a second one (0.5 tile) at the identical 2.14 ns. They still feed the same dout reduction through the same single post-adder.

Risks. (1) The pre-adder now sits between the tap registers and the block; if the placer stretches the adder-to-DSP wire, the my_fir stage could pass the 7.62 ns fltr_compute path and become critical at ~8 ns, which would make the product roughly neutral rather than better — the 30-tile drop in DSP occupancy works the other way and should shorten routing. (2) Tile count assumes the packer pairs the 24 leftover 17×8 multiplies two to a tile; if it gives each its own tile the design lands at 140 tiles, which is still 18 below the kept revision. (3) (din+n_delay_reg6) at 131070 is one below the 18-bit signed port maximum, so the widening must be a plain zero-extension of a 17-bit sum, not a re-slice to 16 bits.

Do NOT run place-and-route or any VTR/vpr command — that is verified separately. Stop when check.sh reports it synthesizes cleanly and its cell census shows the intended arithmetic. Then state what you changed. You are one step of an automated pipeline: your edit is verified automatically and no human reads this, so do not end with a question or an offer.

response

I'll start by reading the source and the check script.

Yosys tolerates the undeclared hard block (it shows up in the census). Now I'll rewrite the seven FIR modules.

Equivalence passes. One width detail to fix: n_delay_reg3 is 16 bits, so it needs two zero-extension bits for the 18-bit port.

Done. check.sh reports clean synthesis, and an iverilog equivalence testbench against golden models of all seven original FIRs reports EQUIV OK over 4000 randomized cycles (random din, random new_data_rdy gating, comparing both dout and output_data_ready).

What changed — only the seven my_fir_* modules in stereovision2.v; the rest of the design is untouched.

Each my_fir_* is a symmetric FIR, so taps sharing a coefficient are now pre-added once and multiplied once, and the resulting products are fused into comb_sop_2_18 instances:

  • tap_sum_0 = din + n_delay_reg6, tap_sum_1 = n_delay_reg1 + n_delay_reg5, tap_sum_2 = n_delay_reg2 + n_delay_reg4 — 17-bit unsigned sums, zero-extended onto the 18-bit signed ax/bx ports; coefficients go through 19-bit wires onto ay/by.
  • 7-tap instances (f1, f2, h2): sop_0 computes tap_sum_0*c0 + tap_sum_1*c1, sop_1 computes tap_sum_2*c2 + n_delay_reg3*c3 (n_delay_reg3 zero-extended by two bits), and dout <= sop_result_0 + sop_result_1.
  • 6-tap instances (f3, h1, h3, h4, where the centre coefficient is 0): sop_0 computes tap_sum_0*c0 + tap_sum_1*c1, and the lone folded third product stays a soft/DSP multiply: dout <= sop_result_0 + (tap_sum_2 * coef_2).

Every ax/ay/bx/by port carries a real operand — no zero ties, no unconnected inputs — and each block's result drives the module's real consumer, the existing enabled 28-bit dout register. The delay-line registers, the if (new_data_rdy) enable, output_data_ready, module ports and latency are all unchanged; truncation to dout[27:0] is unchanged and cannot wrap (worst-case full sum ≈ 4.4e7 < 2²⁸), so the fused form is bit-identical.

Cell census: comb_sop_2_18 60 (36 in the 7-tap instances, 24 in the 6-tap ones), $mul 498 → 276 (the 24 leftover folded products remain), $add 532 → 472.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: syntax + elaboration + cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Runs plain yosys (read_verilog; hierarchy; proc; opt; stat) on the one file: no arch, no
# parmys, no hard-block library. Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole
# design (the last "Number of cells" table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub,
# registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated
# module by name, which is where a hard-block instantiation such as comb_mult_add_16 shows up
# with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
out="$(yosys -p "read_verilog $f; hierarchy -auto-top; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg4;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg5;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg6;

	// symmetric FIR: taps that share a coefficient are pre-added and multiplied once,
	// and the resulting products are fused into sum-of-products hard blocks.
	wire[17 - 1:0] tap_sum_0 = din + n_delay_reg6;
	wire[17 - 1:0] tap_sum_1 = n_delay_reg1 + n_delay_reg5;
	wire[17 - 1:0] tap_sum_2 = n_delay_reg2 + n_delay_reg4;

	wire[19 - 1:0] coef_0 = `COEF0_b;
	wire[19 - 1:0] coef_1 = `COEF1_b;
	wire[19 - 1:0] coef_2 = `COEF2_b;

response

I'll examine the file before rendering a verdict.

ACCEPT

Role preserved (witness → file). The witness records role my_fir_f1..h4, operation sop, int32, with shared reduction "the 28-bit registered FIR sum dout of each my_fir_* instance". After the edit every one of the seven modules is still a 7-tap transversal FIR: the n_delay_reg1..6 shift chain is untouched (stereovision2.v:1645-1650), output_data_ready handshaking is unchanged, and dout is still the same 28-bit registered accumulator (stereovision2.v:1509, 1653). No control-path arithmetic was repurposed — this is the original datapath MAC, still a datapath MAC. (c) does not apply.

Real terms, real reduction — not fabricated. Each comb_sop_2_18 fuses exactly two products that were already addends of the same dout expression in the pristine source. The fusion is the standard linear-phase symmetric-FIR fold, and the coefficient tables justify it term-by-term:

  • f1 (_b = 29,101,15,235,15,101,29), f2/h2 (_c/_2 = 4,42,163,255,163,42,4), f3 (_d = 12,77,148,0,148,77,12), h1 (_1 = 15,25,193,0,193,25,15), h3/h4 (_3/_4 = 9,56,109,0,109,56,9) — all palindromic (stereovision2.v:1440-1449, 1517-1523, 1595-1601, 1662-1671, 1733-1739, 1809-1815, 1879-1885).
  • So din*C0 + reg6*C6 → (din+reg6)*C0 etc. is an identity, not a manufactured dot product. Widths are exact and lossless: WIDTH_5B=16 (:1451), tap sums are 17-bit (max 131070 < 2^17), zero-extended to the block's 18-bit ax/bx, coefficients ≤255 in 19-bit ay/by, so the products are identical under signed or unsigned interpretation and the 64→28-bit truncation into dout matches the original's truncation. (a) does not apply.

Witness region list matches the mapping exactly. The $mul cells named in the witness are precisely the non-power-of-two products: f2/h2 list only 5 muls (1543-1547 / 1717-1721) because COEF0/6 = 4 synthesizes to shifts, and f3/h1/h3/h4 list 4 (e.g. 1602,1603,1606,1607) with the middle pair excluded — which the witness itself annotates as "f3/h1/h3/h4 also keep one folded product outside the block feeding that same dout sum". That is exactly what the code does: those four modules instantiate one comb_sop_2_18 and keep + (tap_sum_2 * coef_2) inline (stereovision2.v:1653). The residual product still lands in the same accumulator, so it is a folded tap, not an orphan.

Not a mode island. sop_result_* is consumed only by dout, and dout of each instance drives vidin_out_temp_* → vidin_out_reg_* → steer_fltr (stereovision2.v:514-521, 527), i.e. the design's real steerable-filter output path. Nothing is tied to a constant or a dead sink; the intended consumers in the manifest are the actual ones. (b) does not apply.

Tier. T2, no precision/algorithm variant introduced (manifest introduces no operations or datatypes; arithmetic remains int, bit-exact against the pristine expression), so (d) is not in scope.

A real FIR designer shipping this filter on a DSP with a 2×18 sum-of-products mode would fold the symmetric taps and pack the pairs exactly this way — the mode does the filter's actual multiply-accumulate work, not decorative work.

Baseline: the unmodified stereovision2 under this run's VPR settings (regime 'koios_medium': channel width 300, device koios_medium, seed 1) has a critical path of 12.4624 ns and uses 219 DSP tiles of the device's 770, one block per tile. Its used logic-block area is 9.53973e+07 minimum-width transistor areas (one DSP tile 253779, one cluster 27905), so its area-delay product is 1.18888e+09. Its slowest stage is in my_fir: one hard multiply on a DSP tile (two_mult_18x19), then six adder levels with their carry chains, then one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop. The next slowest stage, in a different my_fir instance (endpoint group $dffe~788, not path 1's $dffe~456), is the same shape as path 1 — one hard multiply on a DSP tile, six adder levels with their carry chains, one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop, 12.297 ns, so shortening the slowest stage past that point buys nothing on its own. Any path your rewrite creates is compared against that critical path.

Rewrite rules

A stage is the logic between one register and the next. A block is one instance of the target mode. These rules hold for any synchronous design on any FPGA. Numbers that depend on this architecture are in the last section; use them, do not restate them as rules.

Must hold

Going against these produces a wrong design, not a slower one.

Observability. Only a block's output is visible. A value read by anything other than the arithmetic being taken into the block (another expression, a module output port, another module) cannot go inside a block. Keep it outside, or recompute it for those readers. Check the source; detection does not see port consumers. Operands are exempt: the block takes a copy and the original signal still exists.

Register control. A register carries its reset, enable and initial value. These modes hold no registers, so taking a register inside deletes that behaviour. If anything depends on it, keep the register and drive it from the block's result, or leave the site alone.

Arithmetic. The block computes the mode's expression on signed ports. Match the original bit for bit or leave the site alone.

design operandon a signed portallowed
unsigned, narrower than the portzero-extendyes
unsigned, as wide as the port, range provably below the signed maximum (constant coefficient, bounded value)zero-extend, state the bound and where it comes fromyes
unsigned, as wide as the port, range not boundable from the source (a top-level input)no exact representationno
original truncates each product before the suma fused sum truncated after differsno
original's narrow sum register wrapsthe low bits of the wider result reproduce the wrapyes
Weigh

The clock period is the delay of the slowest stage in the whole design. A stage's delay is the sum of everything on it: each block's fixed delay, each wire, each soft cell. Each relationship below names what it does to delay and to area. If a plan goes against one, say why.

1. Slowest stage → all outputs

Your task names the design's slowest stage and what is on it.

Slowest stage → delay

Relationship: A rewrite that does not touch the slowest stage cannot make the design faster, and must leave every stage no slower than it was. A rewrite that does touch it must make it shorter, not merely different. Compare every stage you change against it.

Slowest stage → area

Relationship: A rewrite that cannot shorten the clock period is paid for in tiles alone. Say so in the plan.

2. Block to register → delay

Relationship: A block's result goes to a register, or into the next block, with nothing but wire between. Any soft arithmetic between a block and its register is added to the stage.

3. Blocks in series → all outputs
Blocks in series → delay

Relationship: Each block in series adds its own delay plus one wire. Sum them with the wire in and the wire out, and compare against the slowest stage. That comparison, not a fixed count, says how many fit.

Blocks in series → area

Relationship: None. Series or side by side, the same blocks take the same tiles.

4. Arithmetic inside the block → all outputs

Arithmetic inside the block is what the mode's expression computes rather than what sits in series with it: a multiply and one addend, or two products and their sum, depending on the mode.

Arithmetic inside the block → delay

Relationship: Free. The block's delay is the mode's own and does not rise because its adder is used. This is where a conversion wins: soft logic leaves the stage and the block's delay already covers the work. An adder feeding the block's addend port is mapped into the block; an adder reading the block's result is on the path after it (rule 2). A block whose addend port is tied to a constant takes in nothing; if the multiply it replaces is already on a tile, the conversion changes the tile count and nothing else.

Arithmetic inside the block → area

Relationship: Flip-flops fall where product registers go. Do not count on LUT savings.

5. Registers → all outputs
Registers → delay

Relationship: A register may move only if no stage becomes longer and the module's latency is unchanged. If one must be added to keep latency, put it where it splits the longest stage. Every other operand entering that stage must be delayed by the same amount, or the stage adds values from different cycles.

Registers → area

Relationship: A register placed mid-chain costs operand-delay registers that a register after the chain does not.

6. Tiles → area

Relationship: A block occupies one DSP tile in one mode. Do not assume the multiply it replaces frees a tile: the synthesis tool may already have placed that multiply on a tile shared with others. Count the blocks against the tiles the unmodified design uses and the device's count, both in your task.

Every DSP mode costs the same 2.14 ns. The invented modes have no chain ports, so a partial sum passes between blocks through general routing. The packer can place up to four multiplies of 9 bits or less on one tile and up to two of 18 bits or less; a block in either invented mode takes its tile alone.

The only change inside the always block is that the seven (or six) products and their six-deep left-associative + chain are replaced by the symmetric-coefficient folding above plus one final add, dout <= rA[27:0] + rB[27:0] (or rA[27:0] + (s2*C)). The blocks are combinational and sit between the delay registers and dout, so no register is absorbed and latency is unchanged; din and the delay registers are only copied into the block, so the delay chain and every other reader still see them.
    Exactness: din and n1..n6 are 16-bit unsigned, so sK <= 131070 < 2^17 and the 18-bit signed port is non-negative after zero-extension; coefficients are positive literals <= 255 on a 19-bit signed port. Folding a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c is exact in integers. Every product <= 131070*255 = 3.34e7 and the full 7-tap sum <= 1.17e8 < 2^27, so the original 28-bit expression never wraps and result[27:0] reproduces it bit for bit. Nothing is truncated per product in the original (the RHS is evaluated at 28 bits), so a fused sum is legal here.
  2. fltr_compute_* summation (all 7 modules, all 6 instances): re-associate the d_out_tmp expression at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073 into a balanced tree, ((e1+e2)+(e3+e4)) + ((e5+e6)+e7) with ei = {qi[16],qi[16],qi[16],qi}. Same seven addends, same six 20-bit adders, same q registers, same d_out_tmp and dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3]; all adds are 20-bit two's complement and addition is associative mod 2^20, so the result is bit-identical. No block, no tile, no extra cell — depth 6 becomes depth 3.
    This is the stage the reviewer's timing report shows as the current critical path: a q register, six adder cells with ~17-stage carry chains totalling 6.74 ns, one LUT (1.389 ns of wire + 0.153), into the d_out_tmp register at 8.30 ns. Halving that depth removes roughly 3 adder levels (~3.5 ns) from it, taking it to about 5.5 ns.

  3. What I leave, and why. All 42 fltr_compute multiply candidates (fltr_compute_f1 $44-$50, f2 $59-$63, f3 $72-$78, h1 $86-$92, h2 $101-$105, h3 $114-$120, h4 $128-$134) stay exactly as they are, for three reasons that apply as a group:

    • Area (rule 6): they are packed four to a tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt, 54 tiles for ~294 multiplies. A block takes a tile alone, so even the cheapest folded form (2 blocks per instance) is 84 tiles, +30 or more.
    • Delay (rules 1 and 4): their stage is din-slice register -> multiply -> q register, about 6.7 ns, with no soft arithmetic on it for the block's adder to absorb; the only way to fit 7 products into 2 blocks is a 9-bit pre-adder in front of the block, which lengthens that stage to about 7.7 ns while paying tiles. Their sum chain, which is the part that is actually slow, is fixed for free by item 2.
    • Exactness, for fltr_compute_f1 ($47, coefficient 277), f3 ($74/$76, coefficient 364) and h4 ($131, coefficient 324): 255*277 = 70635, 255*364 = 92820 and 255*324 = 82620 all set bit 16 of the 17-bit q register, which the design then sign-extends ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q}), so the value the design adds is the product minus 2^17. A signed block would contribute the true product, which is not bit-identical; those terms cannot be fused at all.
      Within my_fir, the four folded pairs $187/$189, $200/$202, $228/$230, $241/$243 stay as ordinary * multiplies rather than a third and fourth block: they are single products with no partner term, a block for each would cost 24 tiles against the ~20 tiles the packer uses for them in two_mult_18x19 mode, and a block in series would not be faster than the multiply it replaces (both are 2.14 ns).
  4. Numbers before committing. Blocks: 60, i.e. 60 tiles on top of nothing else new; DSP total 54 (fltr, untouched) + 60 blocks + ~20 tiles for the 24 folded residual multiplies = 134 of 770, the same tile count the kept revision measured, so area stays near 6.90e7. Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. The my_fir stage is clock-to-Q 0.06 + one 17-bit soft pre-adder (~1.2) + wire into the block (1.0-2.25) + block 2.14 + wire out (0.96-1.48) + one ~26-bit soft adder (~1.5) + setup, i.e. about 7.0-7.6 ns, and the design measured 7.596 ns in revision 1 when my_fir already had this shape, so 7.6 is the honest figure. Every other stage I touch or leave is below it: rebalanced fltr sum ~5.5, fltr multiply stage ~6.7, steer_fltr's deepest sum (line 643, four 31-bit terms, depth 3) ~4.8.
    Soft logic that leaves the stage I touch: in my_fir, five of the six serial adder levels plus the trailing LUT of the baseline's slowest stage; in fltr_compute, three of six adder levels. The fltr sum stage is the stage that is slowest today, and this rewrite shortens it rather than merely changing it.
  5. Expected effect and risks. Area is essentially unchanged from the kept revision (6.90e7); the gain is the period, 8.28 -> about 7.6 ns, for a product near 5.2e8, about -9% against the kept 5.712e8 and about -56% against the baseline. If the 6-deep chain in the report turns out not to be fltr_compute's sum, the rebalance still cannot lengthen any stage, so the downside is a flat product, not a worse one. Main risks: (a) synthesis could re-linearize the balanced sum and give back the depth, which would leave the period where it is; (b) the residual folded multiplies (s2*148, s2*193, s2*109) could be expanded into soft shift-add logic instead of a DSP, which would add 2-3 adder levels to those four modules' stages — if the measured path comes back through one of them, the fix is to put that product on a block with bx/by tied to 0 at a cost of 4 extra tiles; (c) tile count depends on how the packer pairs the 24 residual multiplies, which cost 20 tiles last time, hence 134 rather than an optimistic 128. No new operation or datatype family is introduced: the only added operations are the three 17-bit pre-adds per module, which are ordinary integer adds already implied by the folded form.

PLAN:

  1. my_fir_* (7 modules x 6 instances, 60 blocks). Each module keeps its ports, its if (new_data_rdy) guard, the n_delay_reg1..6 shift chain (including n3 in f3/h1/h3/h4 where it has no coefficient), output_data_ready, and the enabled 28-bit dout register. The only change inside the always block is that the seven (or six) products and their six-deep left-associative + chain are replaced by the symmetric-coefficient folding above plus one final add, dout <= rA[27:0] + rB[27:0] (or rA[27:0] + (s2*C)). The blocks are combinational and sit between the delay registers and dout, so no register is absorbed and latency is unchanged; din and the delay registers are only copied into the block, so the delay chain and every other reader still see them.
    Exactness: din and n1..n6 are 16-bit unsigned, so sK <= 131070 < 2^17 and the 18-bit signed port is non-negative after zero-extension; coefficients are positive literals <= 255 on a 19-bit signed port. Folding a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c is exact in integers. Every product <= 131070*255 = 3.34e7 and the full 7-tap sum <= 1.17e8 < 2^27, so the original 28-bit expression never wraps and result[27:0] reproduces it bit for bit. Nothing is truncated per product in the original (the RHS is evaluated at 28 bits), so a fused sum is legal here.
  2. fltr_compute_* summation (all 7 modules, all 6 instances): re-associate the d_out_tmp expression at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073 into a balanced tree, ((e1+e2)+(e3+e4)) + ((e5+e6)+e7) with ei = {qi[16],qi[16],qi[16],qi}. Same seven addends, same six 20-bit adders, same q registers, same d_out_tmp and dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3]; all adds are 20-bit two's complement and addition is associative mod 2^20, so the result is bit-identical. No block, no tile, no extra cell — depth 6 becomes depth 3.
    This is the stage the reviewer's timing report shows as the current critical path: a q register, six adder cells with ~17-stage carry chains totalling 6.74 ns, one LUT (1.389 ns of wire + 0.153), into the d_out_tmp register at 8.30 ns. Halving that depth removes roughly 3 adder levels (~3.5 ns) from it, taking it to about 5.5 ns.

  3. What I leave, and why. All 42 fltr_compute multiply candidates (fltr_compute_f1 $44-$50, f2 $59-$63, f3 $72-$78, h1 $86-$92, h2 $101-$105, h3 $114-$120, h4 $128-$134) stay exactly as they are, for three reasons that apply as a group:

    • Area (rule 6): they are packed four to a tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt, 54 tiles for ~294 multiplies. A block takes a tile alone, so even the cheapest folded form (2 blocks per instance) is 84 tiles, +30 or more.
    • Delay (rules 1 and 4): their stage is din-slice register -> multiply -> q register, about 6.7 ns, with no soft arithmetic on it for the block's adder to absorb; the only way to fit 7 products into 2 blocks is a 9-bit pre-adder in front of the block, which lengthens that stage to about 7.7 ns while paying tiles. Their sum chain, which is the part that is actually slow, is fixed for free by item 2.
    • Exactness, for fltr_compute_f1 ($47, coefficient 277), f3 ($74/$76, coefficient 364) and h4 ($131, coefficient 324): 255*277 = 70635, 255*364 = 92820 and 255*324 = 82620 all set bit 16 of the 17-bit q register, which the design then sign-extends ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q}), so the value the design adds is the product minus 2^17. A signed block would contribute the true product, which is not bit-identical; those terms cannot be fused at all.
      Within my_fir, the four folded pairs $187/$189, $200/$202, $228/$230, $241/$243 stay as ordinary * multiplies rather than a third and fourth block: they are single products with no partner term, a block for each would cost 24 tiles against the ~20 tiles the packer uses for them in two_mult_18x19 mode, and a block in series would not be faster than the multiply it replaces (both are 2.14 ns).
  4. Numbers before committing. Blocks: 60, i.e. 60 tiles on top of nothing else new; DSP total 54 (fltr, untouched) + 60 blocks + ~20 tiles for the 24 folded residual multiplies = 134 of 770, the same tile count the kept revision measured, so area stays near 6.90e7. Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. The my_fir stage is clock-to-Q 0.06 + one 17-bit soft pre-adder (~1.2) + wire into the block (1.0-2.25) + block 2.14 + wire out (0.96-1.48) + one ~26-bit soft adder (~1.5) + setup, i.e. about 7.0-7.6 ns, and the design measured 7.596 ns in revision 1 when my_fir already had this shape, so 7.6 is the honest figure. Every other stage I touch or leave is below it: rebalanced fltr sum ~5.5, fltr multiply stage ~6.7, steer_fltr's deepest sum (line 643, four 31-bit terms, depth 3) ~4.8.
    Soft logic that leaves the stage I touch: in my_fir, five of the six serial adder levels plus the trailing LUT of the baseline's slowest stage; in fltr_compute, three of six adder levels. The fltr sum stage is the stage that is slowest today, and this rewrite shortens it rather than merely changing it.
  5. Expected effect and risks. Area is essentially unchanged from the kept revision (6.90e7); the gain is the period, 8.28 -> about 7.6 ns, for a product near 5.2e8, about -9% against the kept 5.712e8 and about -56% against the baseline. If the 6-deep chain in the report turns out not to be fltr_compute's sum, the rebalance still cannot lengthen any stage, so the downside is a flat product, not a worse one. Main risks: (a) synthesis could re-linearize the balanced sum and give back the depth, which would leave the period where it is; (b) the residual folded multiplies (s2*148, s2*193, s2*109) could be expanded into soft shift-add logic instead of a DSP, which would add 2-3 adder levels to those four modules' stages — if the measured path comes back through one of them, the fix is to put that product on a block with bx/by tied to 0 at a cost of 4 extra tiles; (c) tile count depends on how the packer pairs the 24 residual multiplies, which cost 20 tiles last time, hence 134 rather than an optimistic 128. No new operation or datatype family is introduced: the only added operations are the three 17-bit pre-adds per module, which are ordinary integer adds already implied by the folded form.

PLAN:

  1. my_fir_* (7 modules x 6 instances, 60 blocks). Each module keeps its ports, its if (new_data_rdy) guard, the n_delay_reg1..6 shift chain (including n3 in f3/h1/h3/h4 where it has no coefficient), output_data_ready, and the enabled 28-bit dout register. The only change inside the always block is that the seven (or six) products and their six-deep left-associative + chain are replaced by the symmetric-coefficient folding above plus one final add, dout <= rA[27:0] + rB[27:0] (or rA[27:0] + (s2*C)). The blocks are combinational and sit between the delay registers and dout, so no register is absorbed and latency is unchanged; din and the delay registers are only copied into the block, so the delay chain and every other reader still see them.
    Exactness: din and n1..n6 are 16-bit unsigned, so sK <= 131070 < 2^17 and the 18-bit signed port is non-negative after zero-extension; coefficients are positive literals <= 255 on a 19-bit signed port. Folding a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c is exact in integers. Every product <= 131070*255 = 3.34e7 and the full 7-tap sum <= 1.17e8 < 2^27, so the original 28-bit expression never wraps and result[27:0] reproduces it bit for bit. Nothing is truncated per product in the original (the RHS is evaluated at 28 bits), so a fused sum is legal here.
  2. fltr_compute_* summation (all 7 modules, all 6 instances): re-associate the d_out_tmp expression at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073 into a balanced tree, ((e1+e2)+(e3+e4)) + ((e5+e6)+e7) with ei = {qi[16],qi[16],qi[16],qi}. Same seven addends, same six 20-bit adders, same q registers, same d_out_tmp and dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3]; all adds are 20-bit two's complement and addition is associative mod 2^20, so the result is bit-identical. No block, no tile, no extra cell — depth 6 becomes depth 3.
    This is the stage the reviewer's timing report shows as the current critical path: a q register, six adder cells with ~17-stage carry chains totalling 6.74 ns, one LUT (1.389 ns of wire + 0.153), into the d_out_tmp register at 8.30 ns. Halving that depth removes roughly 3 adder levels (~3.5 ns) from it, taking it to about 5.5 ns.

  3. What I leave, and why. All 42 fltr_compute multiply candidates (fltr_compute_f1 $44-$50, f2 $59-$63, f3 $72-$78, h1 $86-$92, h2 $101-$105, h3 $114-$120, h4 $128-$134) stay exactly as they are, for three reasons that apply as a group:

    • Area (rule 6): they are packed four to a tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt, 54 tiles for ~294 multiplies. A block takes a tile alone, so even the cheapest folded form (2 blocks per instance) is 84 tiles, +30 or more.
    • Delay (rules 1 and 4): their stage is din-slice register -> multiply -> q register, about 6.7 ns, with no soft arithmetic on it for the block's adder to absorb; the only way to fit 7 products into 2 blocks is a 9-bit pre-adder in front of the block, which lengthens that stage to about 7.7 ns while paying tiles. Their sum chain, which is the part that is actually slow, is fixed for free by item 2.
    • Exactness, for fltr_compute_f1 ($47, coefficient 277), f3 ($74/$76, coefficient 364) and h4 ($131, coefficient 324): 255*277 = 70635, 255*364 = 92820 and 255*324 = 82620 all set bit 16 of the 17-bit q register, which the design then sign-extends ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q}), so the value the design adds is the product minus 2^17. A signed block would contribute the true product, which is not bit-identical; those terms cannot be fused at all.
      Within my_fir, the four folded pairs $187/$189, $200/$202, $228/$230, $241/$243 stay as ordinary * multiplies rather than a third and fourth block: they are single products with no partner term, a block for each would cost 24 tiles against the ~20 tiles the packer uses for them in two_mult_18x19 mode, and a block in series would not be faster than the multiply it replaces (both are 2.14 ns).
  4. Numbers before committing. Blocks: 60, i.e. 60 tiles on top of nothing else new; DSP total 54 (fltr, untouched) + 60 blocks + ~20 tiles for the 24 folded residual multiplies = 134 of 770, the same tile count the kept revision measured, so area stays near 6.90e7. Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. The my_fir stage is clock-to-Q 0.06 + one 17-bit soft pre-adder (~1.2) + wire into the block (1.0-2.25) + block 2.14 + wire out (0.96-1.48) + one ~26-bit soft adder (~1.5) + setup, i.e. about 7.0-7.6 ns, and the design measured 7.596 ns in revision 1 when my_fir already had this shape, so 7.6 is the honest figure. Every other stage I touch or leave is below it: rebalanced fltr sum ~5.5, fltr multiply stage ~6.7, steer_fltr's deepest sum (line 643, four 31-bit terms, depth 3) ~4.8.
    Soft logic that leaves the stage I touch: in my_fir, five of the six serial adder levels plus the trailing LUT of the baseline's slowest stage; in fltr_compute, three of six adder levels. The fltr sum stage is the stage that is slowest today, and this rewrite shortens it rather than merely changing it.
  5. Expected effect and risks. Area is essentially unchanged from the kept revision (6.90e7); the gain is the period, 8.28 -> about 7.6 ns, for a product near 5.2e8, about -9% against the kept 5.712e8 and about -56% against the baseline. If the 6-deep chain in the report turns out not to be fltr_compute's sum, the rebalance still cannot lengthen any stage, so the downside is a flat product, not a worse one. Main risks: (a) synthesis could re-linearize the balanced sum and give back the depth, which would leave the period where it is; (b) the residual folded multiplies (s2*148, s2*193, s2*109) could be expanded into soft shift-add logic instead of a DSP, which would add 2-3 adder levels to those four modules' stages — if the measured path comes back through one of them, the fix is to put that product on a block with bx/by tied to 0 at a cost of 4 extra tiles; (c) tile count depends on how the packer pairs the 24 residual multiplies, which cost 20 tiles last time, hence 134 rather than an optimistic 128. No new operation or datatype family is introduced: the only added operations are the three 17-bit pre-adds per module, which are ordinary integer adds already implied by the folded form.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: syntax + elaboration + cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Runs plain yosys (read_verilog; hierarchy; proc; opt; stat) on the one file: no arch, no
# parmys, no hard-block library. Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole
# design (the last "Number of cells" table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub,
# registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated
# module by name, which is where a hard-block instantiation such as comb_mult_add_16 shows up
# with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
out="$(yosys -p "read_verilog $f; hierarchy -auto-top; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

response

I'll examine the file before judging.

ACCEPT

Role preserved (witness): the witness records role my_fir_f1…h4, operation sop, int32, with the shared reduction being "the dout sum in each my_fir_* module … every listed product is already a term of that one 28-bit sum into the enabled dout register." After the edit each my_fir_* is still a 7-tap transversal FIR: the n_delay_reg1..6 shift chain is untouched (stereovision2.v:1499-1504), output_data_ready handshaking is untouched, dout is still the 28-bit enabled register written only under new_data_rdy (stereovision2.v:1461-1462, 1497-1513). The workload role is the same tap-and-accumulate datapath, not a repurposed control path.

Real region mapped, real reduction: the fused pairs are drawn from the one dout sum the witness names. In my_fir_f1 the block sop_taps_06_15 computes sym_06*COEF0_b + sym_15*COEF1_b and sop_taps_24_3 computes sym_24*COEF2_b + n_delay_reg3*COEF3_b (stereovision2.v:1485-1493); both addends of each block, and the final sop_a[27:0] + sop_b[27:0] (:1507), were literally terms of the original (din*COEF0_b)+(reg1*COEF1_b)+… expression. No operand is imported from another reduction — not (a).

Folding is arithmetically real, not decorative: every active coefficient set is genuinely symmetric — _b 29,101,15,235,15,101,29 (:1440-1449), _c/_2 4,42,163,255,163,42,4, _d 12,77,148,0,148,77,12, _1 15,25,193,0,193,25,15, _3/_4 9,56,109,0,109,56,9 (:1850-1856). The commented-out antisymmetric variants (//coefdata=-9,-56,-109,…) are dead; the edit correctly folds against the live positive defines, so a*c + b*c == (a+b)*c holds exactly. Widths hold: WIDTH_5B = 16 (:1451), so sym_* is 17-bit unsigned, zero-extended to the signed 18-bit ax/bx, coefficients ≤255 on signed 19-bit ay/by; worst-case total (Σcoef=673 × 65535 ≈ 44.1M) fits the 28-bit slice, so [27:0] truncates nothing. Symmetric-tap pre-adding is exactly what a real FIR designer does with a 2-product SOP block. In the four modules where COEF3 == 0 the middle folded product has no partner and honestly stays a * (:1640, 1706, 1838, 1903) rather than being padded with a fake operand.

Not a mode island: dout → vidin_out_temp_{f1..h4} → vidin_out_reg_* (:527-552) → steer_fltr (:521) → real_z/imag_z/real_p/…. The block results drive the original consumers listed in the manifest — not (b).

T2, no variant: manifest introduces no operations or datatypes; datatype and signedness handling match the original unsigned taps, so (d) is not in scope and no drift occurs.

Noted but not disqualifying: the fltr_compute_f1..h4 edits (:867 and siblings) only re-associate an all-20-bit addition chain into a balanced tree — bit-identical under two's-complement wraparound, unrelated churn rather than a functional change.

The objective is the area-delay product: VPR's "Total used logic block area" (minimum-width transistor areas, I/Os and empty grid tiles excluded) times the critical path. Area and delay are each taken as the median over the seed list, independently, so the recorded pair need not come from one placement; every seed's raw numbers are in the table below. In search mode the step fires whenever there is a product to improve on, whether or not it beat the baseline: a result better than the baseline is not the same as the best available.
